sentences.zh: 【唐紀四十九】起強圉閼八月，盡重光協洽，凡四年有奇。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 49] Beginning in the eighth month of the year Qiangwu E, ending in Chongguang Xiejia, altogether a little more than four years.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 49] From the eighth month of Qiangwu E through Chongguang Xiejia—four years and change in all.

sentences.zh: 德宗神武聖文皇帝八貞元三年（

translations.literal: The Divine Martial Sage Literary Emperor Dezong, Zhenyuan year three (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong, the Divine Martial and Sage Literary Emperor—Zhenyuan year 3 (

sentences.zh: 丁卯，公元七八七年）

translations.literal: dingmao, CE 787)
translations.idiomatic: dingmao, AD 787)

sentences.zh: 八月，辛巳朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the first day of the month xinsi, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the xinsi new moon, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃尚結贊遣五騎送崔漢衡歸，且上表求和。

translations.literal: The Tibetan minister Shang Jiezan sent five horsemen to escort Cui Hanheng back, and also submitted a memorial seeking peace.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet's Shang Jiezan dispatched five riders to return Cui Hanheng and submitted a memorial requesting peace.

sentences.zh: 至潘原，李觀語之以「有詔不納吐蕃使者」，受其表而卻其人。

translations.literal: When they reached Panyuan, Li Guan told them, "There is an edict not to receive Tibetan envoys," accepted their memorial, and sent the men back.
translations.idiomatic: At Panyuan, Li Guan told them that an edict forbade receiving Tibetan envoys; he took their memorial but turned the envoys away.

sentences.zh: 初，兵部侍郎、同平章事柳渾與張延賞俱為相，渾議事數異同，延賞使所親謂曰：「相公舊德，但節言於廟堂，則重位可久。

translations.literal: Earlier, Vice Minister of War and Fellow Grand Councillor Liu Hun and Zhang Yanshang were both chancellors; Hun often differed with Zhang in council deliberations. Zhang had a confidant say to him, "Your Excellency's long-standing virtue—if you would only moderate your speech in the hall of state, your high office could be prolonged."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Liu Hun and Zhang Yanshang both served as chancellors, Hun often disagreed with Zhang in deliberations. Zhang sent a confidant to say, "Your Excellency's established merit would keep you in high office longer if you spoke more sparingly in court."

sentences.zh: 」渾曰：「為吾謝張公，柳渾頭可斷，舌不可禁！

translations.literal: " Liu Hun said, "Give my thanks to Lord Zhang: Liu Hun's head may be cut off, but his tongue cannot be silenced!"
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Hun replied, "Tell Lord Zhang for me: Liu Hun's head may be severed, but his tongue will not be stilled!"

sentences.zh: 」由是交惡。

translations.literal: " From this their relations turned hostile.
translations.idiomatic: " From that point they became bitter enemies.

sentences.zh: 上好文雅縕藉，而渾質直輕侻，無威儀，於上前時發俚語。

translations.literal: The emperor favored refined elegance and restraint, while Hun was plainspoken, blunt, and light in manner, without dignified bearing, and at times used vulgar speech before the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor prized refined, restrained speech, but Hun was blunt and casual, lacking courtly dignity, and sometimes used colloquial language in his presence.

sentences.zh: 上不悅，欲黜為王府長史，李泌言：「渾褊直無他。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and wished to demote him to chief administrator of a princely establishment. Li Bi said, "Hun is narrow and blunt but has no other fault."
translations.idiomatic: Displeased, the emperor wanted to demote Hun to chief administrator of a princely household. Li Bi said, "Hun is merely narrow and blunt—there is nothing else against him."

sentences.zh: 故事，罷相無為長史者。

translations.literal: By precedent, no dismissed chancellor has ever been made a chief administrator.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, no dismissed chancellor had ever been assigned as a princely chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 」又欲以為王傅，泌請以為常侍，上曰：「苟得罷之，無不可者。

translations.literal: " The emperor then wished to make him a tutor to a prince; Bi asked that he be made an attendant cavalier instead. The emperor said, "So long as I can remove him, anything will do."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then proposed making him a prince's tutor; Bi asked instead for attendant cavalier. The emperor said, "If I can remove him from office, anything will do."

sentences.zh: 」己丑，渾罷為左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: " On the day jichou, Hun was dismissed and made Left Attendant Cavalier at Large.
translations.idiomatic: " On jichou, Hun was removed from the chancellorship and appointed Left Attendant Cavalier at Large.

sentences.zh: 初，郜國大長公主適駙馬都尉蕭升。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Princess of Guo State, Grand Imperial Aunt, had married Commandant of Cavalry Xiao Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Princess of Guo State, a grand imperial aunt, had married Commandant of Cavalry Xiao Sheng.

sentences.zh: 升，復之從兄弟也。

translations.literal: Sheng was a cousin of Emperor Dezong on his mother's side.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was a cousin of Emperor Dezong on the maternal line.

sentences.zh: 公主不謹，詹事李升、蜀州別駕蕭鼎、彭州司馬李萬、豐陽令韋恪，皆出入主第。

translations.literal: The princess was indiscreet; Chamberlain Li Sheng, Acting Governor of Shu Prefecture Xiao Ding, Secretary of Peng Prefecture Li Wan, and Magistrate of Fengyang Wei Ke all came and went at her residence.
translations.idiomatic: The princess conducted herself loosely; Chamberlain Li Sheng, Acting Governor of Shu Xiao Ding, Secretary of Peng Li Wan, and Magistrate of Fengyang Wei Ke all frequented her mansion.

sentences.zh: 主女為太子妃，始者上恩禮甚厚，主常直乘肩輿抵東宮。

translations.literal: The princess's daughter was the crown prince's consort; at first the emperor's favor and courtesy were very great, and the princess often rode in a palanquin straight to the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Her daughter was crown princess; at first the emperor showed her great favor, and she often took a palanquin directly to the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 宗戚皆疾之。

translations.literal: The imperial clansmen all resented this.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial kin all resented her.

sentences.zh: 或告主淫亂，且為厭禱。

translations.literal: Someone reported that the princess was licentious and also practiced malign sorcery.
translations.idiomatic: Someone accused the princess of sexual misconduct and of practicing malign sorcery against the court.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，幽主於禁中，切責太子。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered, confined the princess within the palace precincts, and sternly rebuked the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage, confined the princess within the palace, and sharply rebuked the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 太子不知所對，請與蕭妃離婚。

translations.literal: The crown prince did not know how to reply and asked to divorce Consort Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince did not know how to answer and asked to divorce Consort Xiao.

sentences.zh: 上召李泌告之，且曰：「舒王近已長立，孝友溫仁。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Li Bi and told him, saying also, "Prince Shu has lately come of age; he is filial, friendly, gentle, and benevolent."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Li Bi and told him, adding, "Prince Shu has lately come of age—filial, friendly, gentle, and benevolent."

sentences.zh: 」泌曰：「何至於是！

translations.literal: " Bi said, "How can it come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: " Bi said, "How can matters have come to this!"

sentences.zh: 陛下惟有一子，奈何一旦疑之，欲廢之而立侄，得無失計乎！

translations.literal: Your Majesty has only one son—how can you suddenly suspect him, wish to depose him and establish a nephew? Is this not a grave miscalculation!"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has only one son. How can you suddenly doubt him, depose him, and set up a nephew? Would that not be a grave mistake?"

sentences.zh: 」上勃然怒曰：「卿何得間人父子！

translations.literal: " The emperor flushed with anger and said, "How dare you come between a father and son!"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor flared up in anger. "How dare you drive a wedge between father and son!"

sentences.zh: 誰語卿舒王為侄者？

translations.literal: Who told you that Prince Shu is a nephew?"
translations.idiomatic: Who told you Prince Shu was a nephew?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「陛下自言之。

translations.literal: " He replied, "Your Majesty said it yourself."
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "Your Majesty said so yourself."

sentences.zh: 大歷初，陛下語臣，『今日得數子』。

translations.literal: In the early Dali era Your Majesty told me, 'Today I have gained several sons.'"
translations.idiomatic: In the early Dali reign you told me, 'Today I have gained several sons.'"

sentences.zh: 臣請其故，陛下言『昭靖諸子，主上令吾子之。

translations.literal: I asked the reason, and Your Majesty said, 'The sons of Prince Zhaojing—the late emperor ordered me to treat them as my sons.'"
translations.idiomatic: When I asked why, you said, 'The sons of Prince Zhaojing—the late emperor ordered me to treat them as my own sons.'"

sentences.zh: 』今陛下所生之子猶疑之，何有於侄！

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty even doubts the son you bore yourself—how much less a nephew!"
translations.idiomatic: If you doubt even your own son, how much less should you trust a nephew!"

sentences.zh: 舒王雖孝，自今陛下宜努力，勿復望其孝矣！

translations.literal: Though Prince Shu is filial, from now on Your Majesty should exert yourself and no longer expect his filial piety!"
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shu may be filial now, but from this day forward Your Majesty should not count on his filial devotion!"

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「卿不愛家族乎？

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "Do you not care for your clan?"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Do you not care for your own family?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣惟愛家族，故不敢不盡言。

translations.literal: " He replied, "It is precisely because I care for my clan that I dare not fail to speak fully."
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "It is precisely because I love my family that I dare not hold back."

sentences.zh: 若畏陛下盛怒而為曲從，陛下明日悔之，必尤臣云：『吾獨任汝為相，不力諫，使至此，必復殺而子。

translations.literal: If I feared Your Majesty's great wrath and bent to please you, when Your Majesty repented tomorrow you would surely blame me, saying, 'I alone entrusted you as chancellor; you did not remonstrate forcefully and let matters come to this—you will surely kill your sons again.'"
translations.idiomatic: If I feared your wrath and flattered you, when you repented tomorrow you would blame me: 'I alone made you chancellor; you did not remonstrate forcefully and let matters come to this—you will kill your sons again.'"

sentences.zh: 』臣老矣，餘年不足惜，若冤殺臣子，使臣以侄為嗣，臣未知得歆其祀乎！

translations.literal: I am old; the years left me are not worth sparing. But if my sons were killed unjustly and I had to take a nephew as heir, I do not know whether I would receive offerings at my shrine!"
translations.idiomatic: I am old; my remaining years are not worth sparing. But if my sons were killed unjustly and I had to adopt a nephew as heir, I do not know whether my sacrifices would be honored!"

sentences.zh: 」因嗚咽流涕。

translations.literal: " With this he sobbed and wept.
translations.idiomatic: " With that he sobbed and wept.

sentences.zh: 上亦泣曰：「事已如此，使朕如何而可？

translations.literal: The emperor also wept and said, "Matters have already come to this—what can I do?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept as well. "Matters have already come to this—what can I do?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「此大事，願陛下審圖之。

translations.literal: " He replied, "This is a great matter; I beg Your Majesty to consider it carefully."
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "This is a grave matter. I beg Your Majesty to weigh it carefully."

sentences.zh: 臣始謂陛下聖德，當使海外蠻夷皆戴之如父母，豈謂自有子而疑之至此乎！

translations.literal: I had thought Your Majesty's sage virtue would make even foreign barbarians beyond the seas revere you as parents—who would have thought that with a son of your own you would doubt him to this degree!"
translations.idiomatic: I had thought your sage virtue would make even distant barbarians revere you as parents—who would have thought you would doubt your own son to this degree!"

sentences.zh: 臣今盡言，不敢避忌諱。

translations.literal: I now speak fully and dare not avoid taboo subjects.
translations.idiomatic: I speak fully now and dare not avoid forbidden topics.

sentences.zh: 自古父子相疑，未有不亡國覆家者。

translations.literal: From antiquity, whenever father and son doubted each other, there has never failed to be ruin of state and destruction of family.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity, whenever father and son doubted each other, state and family alike were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 陛下記昔在彭原，建寧何故而誅？

translations.literal: Does Your Majesty remember when you were at Pengyuan—why was Prince Jianning executed?"
translations.idiomatic: Does Your Majesty remember Pengyuan—why was Prince Jianning executed?"

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「建寧叔實冤，肅宗性急，譖之者深耳！

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "Uncle Jianning was truly wronged; Emperor Suzong was hasty by nature, and the slanderers went very deep!"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Uncle Jianning was truly wronged. Suzong was hasty by nature, and the slander ran very deep!"

sentences.zh: 」泌曰：「臣昔以建寧之故，固辭官爵，誓不近天子左右。

translations.literal: " Bi said, "Because of Jianning I once firmly declined rank and title, swearing never again to approach the Son of Heaven's side."
translations.idiomatic: " Bi said, "Because of Jianning I once firmly declined office and swore never again to approach the throne."

sentences.zh: 不幸今日復為陛下相，又睹茲事。

translations.literal: Alas, today I am again Your Majesty's chancellor and witness this affair once more.
translations.idiomatic: Alas, today I am again your chancellor and witness this affair once more.

sentences.zh: 臣在彭原，承恩無比，竟不敢言建寧之冤，及臨辭乃言之，肅宗亦悔而泣。

translations.literal: At Pengyuan I received favor beyond compare, yet I still did not dare speak of Jianning's injustice; only when taking leave did I speak of it, and Suzong too repented and wept.
translations.idiomatic: At Pengyuan I received favor beyond compare, yet I still did not dare speak of Jianning's injustice; only when taking leave did I speak of it, and Suzong too repented and wept.

sentences.zh: 先帝自建寧之死，常懷危懼，臣亦為先帝誦《黃台瓜辭》以防讒構之端。

translations.literal: After Jianning's death the late emperor constantly lived in dread; I also recited for him the 'Melon of Huangtai' poem to guard against the beginnings of slanderous plotting.
translations.idiomatic: After Jianning's death the late emperor lived in constant dread; I also recited for him the 'Melon of Huangtai' poem to guard against the beginnings of slander.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「朕固知之。

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "I have always known this."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "I have always known that."

sentences.zh: 」意色稍解，乃曰：「貞觀、開元皆易太子，何故不亡？

translations.literal: His expression eased somewhat, and he then said, "In the Zhenguan and Kaiyuan reigns they both replaced crown princes—why did the dynasty not perish?"
translations.idiomatic: His expression eased somewhat. "In Zhenguan and Kaiyuan they both replaced crown princes—why did the dynasty not perish?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣方欲言之。

translations.literal: " He replied, "I was just about to speak of that."
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "I was just about to speak of that."

sentences.zh: 昔承乾屢嘗監國，托附者眾，東宮甲士甚多，與宰相侯君集謀反，事覺，太宗使其舅長孫無忌與朝臣數十人鞫之，事狀顯白，然後集百官而議之。

translations.literal: In the past Chengqian had repeatedly acted as regent; those who attached themselves to him were many, and the Eastern Palace had a great host of armored soldiers. He plotted rebellion with Chancellor Hou Junji; when the affair was exposed, Taizong had his maternal uncle Zhangsun Wuji and several dozen court officials interrogate him until the facts were fully clear, and only then convened all officials to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: In the past Chengqian had repeatedly acted as regent; many attached themselves to him, and the Eastern Palace had a large force of armored soldiers. He plotted rebellion with Chancellor Hou Junji; when the affair was exposed, Taizong had his maternal uncle Zhangsun Wuji and dozens of court officials interrogate him until the facts were fully clear, and only then convened all officials to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 當時言者猶云：『願陛下不失為慈父，使太子得終天年。

translations.literal: Even then speakers still said, 'We hope Your Majesty will not cease to be a loving father and will let the crown prince live out his natural span.'"
translations.idiomatic: Even then speakers still said, 'We hope Your Majesty will not cease to be a loving father and will let the crown prince live out his natural span.'"

sentences.zh: 』太宗從之，並廢魏王泰。

translations.literal: Taizong followed this counsel and also deposed Prince Wei Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong followed this counsel and also deposed Prince Wei Tai.

sentences.zh: 陛下既知肅宗性急，以建寧為冤，臣不勝慶幸。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty already knows that Suzong was hasty by nature and that Jianning was wronged, I cannot contain my rejoicing.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty already knows Suzong was hasty by nature and that Jianning was wronged, I cannot contain my rejoicing.

sentences.zh: 願陛下戒覆車之失，從容三日，究其端緒而思之，陛下必釋然知太子之無它矣。

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to guard against repeating a overturned cart's mistake, take three days at ease, trace the matter to its roots and reflect on it—Your Majesty will surely be relieved to know the crown prince has no other intent.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to learn from overturned carts, take three days at ease, trace the matter to its roots and reflect on it—Your Majesty will surely be relieved to know the crown prince has no other intent.

sentences.zh: 若果有其跡，當召大臣知義理者二十人與臣鞫其左右，必有實狀，願陛下如貞觀之法行之，並廢舒王而立皇孫，則百代之後，有天下者猶陛下子孫也。

translations.literal: If there truly are traces of guilt, summon twenty great ministers who understand principle and right conduct, together with me, to interrogate those around him—there will surely be solid facts. I beg Your Majesty to act as in the Zhenguan precedent, also deposing Prince Shu and establishing the imperial grandson; then a hundred generations hence whoever holds the realm will still be Your Majesty's descendants.
translations.idiomatic: If there truly are traces of guilt, summon twenty great ministers who understand principle and right conduct, together with me, to interrogate those around him—there will surely be solid facts. I beg Your Majesty to act as in the Zhenguan precedent, also deposing Prince Shu and establishing the imperial grandson; then a hundred generations hence whoever holds the realm will still be Your Majesty's descendants.

sentences.zh: 至於開元之時，武惠妃譖太子瑛兄弟殺之，海內冤憤，此乃百代所當戒，又可法乎！

translations.literal: As for the Kaiyuan period, Consort Wu Huifei slandered Crown Prince Ying and his brothers until they were killed; throughout the realm there was wrongful indignation—this is what a hundred generations ought to take warning from. How can it be taken as a model!"
translations.idiomatic: As for Kaiyuan, Consort Wu Huifei slandered Crown Prince Ying and his brothers until they were killed; throughout the realm there was wrongful indignation—this is what a hundred generations ought to take warning from. How can it be taken as a model!"

sentences.zh: 且陛下昔嘗令太子見臣於蓬萊池，觀其容表，非有蜂目豺聲商臣之相也，正恐失於柔仁耳。

translations.literal: Moreover, Your Majesty once had the crown prince meet me at Penglai Pool so I might observe his bearing—he does not have the look of wasp eyes and jackal voice like the minister Shang. I only fear he errs on the side of excessive gentleness and benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Your Majesty once had the crown prince meet me at Penglai Pool so I might observe his bearing—he does not have the look of wasp eyes and jackal voice like the minister Shang. I only fear he errs on the side of excessive gentleness and benevolence.

sentences.zh: 又，太子自貞元以來常居少陽院，在寢殿之側，未嘗接外人，預外事，安有異謀乎！

translations.literal: Again, since the Zhenyuan era the crown prince has constantly resided in the Shaoyang Courtyard beside the sleeping hall; he has never received outsiders or taken part in external affairs—how could there be a divergent plot!"
translations.idiomatic: Again, since Zhenyuan the crown prince has constantly resided in the Shaoyang Courtyard beside the sleeping hall; he has never received outsiders or taken part in external affairs—how could there be a divergent plot!"

sentences.zh: 彼譖人者巧詐百端，雖有手書如晉愍懷，衷甲如太子瑛，猶未可信，況但以妻母有罪為累乎！

translations.literal: Those who slander are crafty in a hundred ways; even if there were a handwritten letter like that of Jin's Prince Minhuai, or hidden armor like Crown Prince Ying's, it would still not be credible—how much less when the charge is merely that his wife's mother is guilty!"
translations.idiomatic: Slanderers are crafty in a hundred ways; even a handwritten letter like Jin's Prince Minhuai's, or hidden armor like Crown Prince Ying's, would still not be credible—how much less when the charge is merely that his wife's mother is guilty!"

sentences.zh: 幸陛下語臣，臣敢以家族保太子必不知謀。

translations.literal: Fortunately Your Majesty spoke to me; I dare pledge my clan that the crown prince surely knows nothing of plotting.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately Your Majesty spoke to me; I dare pledge my clan that the crown prince surely knows nothing of plotting.

sentences.zh: 曏使楊素、許敬宗、李林甫之徒承此旨，已就舒王圖定策之功矣！

translations.literal: Had men like Yang Su, Xu Jingzong, or Li Linfu received such an intent, they would already have completed the merit of fixing the succession for Prince Shu!"
translations.idiomatic: Had men like Yang Su, Xu Jingzong, or Li Linfu received such an intent, they would already have fixed the succession for Prince Shu!"

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「朕父子賴卿得全，方屬子孫，使卿代代富貴以報德，何為出此言乎！

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "My son and I owe our preservation to you. I entrust my descendants to you and will make your line wealthy generation after generation to repay your virtue—why speak such words!"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "My son and I owe our preservation to you. I entrust my descendants to you and will make your line wealthy generation after generation to repay your virtue—why speak such words!"

sentences.zh: 」甲午，詔李萬不知避宗，宜杖死，李升等及公主五子，皆流嶺南及遠州。

translations.literal: " On the day jiawu an edict declared that Li Wan, for not knowing how to avoid the imperial clan, should be beaten to death; Li Sheng and the others, and the princess's five sons, were all exiled to Lingnan and distant prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: " On jiawu an edict declared Li Wan, for not knowing how to avoid the imperial clan, should be beaten to death; Li Sheng and the others, and the princess's five sons, were all exiled to Lingnan and distant prefectures.

sentences.zh: 戊申，吐蕃帥羌、渾之眾寇隴州，連營數十里，京城震恐。

translations.literal: On the day wushen the Tibetans led Qiang and Hun forces to raid Long Prefecture, pitching camps in a chain several tens of li long; the capital was shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Tibet led Qiang and Hun forces against Long Prefecture, pitching camps in a chain several tens of li long; the capital was shaken with fear.

sentences.zh: 九月，丁卯，遣神策將石季章戍武功，決勝軍使唐良臣戍百里城。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day dingmao, the Shence general Shi Jizhang was sent to garrison Wugong, and the Victorious Army commissioner Tang Liangchen to garrison Baili City.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on dingmao, Shence general Shi Jizhang was sent to garrison Wugong, and Victorious Army commissioner Tang Liangchen to garrison Baili City.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，吐蕃大掠汧陽、吳山、華亭，老弱者殺之，或斷手鑿目，棄之而去，驅丁壯萬餘悉送安化峽西，將分隸羌、渾，乃告之曰：「聽爾東向哭辭鄉國。

translations.literal: On the day dingsi the Tibetans greatly plundered Qianyang, Wushan, and Huating; the old and weak they killed, some having hands cut off and eyes gouged out before being abandoned. They drove more than ten thousand able-bodied men west of Anhua Gorge to be apportioned among the Qiang and Hun, then told them, "We allow you to face east and weep farewell to your native land."
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi Tibet raided Qianyang, Wushan, and Huating on a great scale; the old and weak they killed, some with hands cut off and eyes gouged out before being abandoned. They drove more than ten thousand able-bodied men west of Anhua Gorge to be apportioned among the Qiang and Hun, then told them, "You may face east and weep farewell to your native land."

sentences.zh: 」眾大哭，赴崖谷死傷者千餘人。

translations.literal: " The multitude wept loudly; more than a thousand threw themselves into cliffs and ravines, dead or injured.
translations.idiomatic: " The multitude wept loudly; more than a thousand threw themselves into cliffs and ravines, dead or injured.

sentences.zh: 未幾，吐蕃之眾復至，圍隴州，刺史韓清沔與神策副將蘇太平夜出兵擊卻之。

translations.literal: Before long the Tibetan host came again, besieging Long Prefecture; Prefect Han Qingmian and Shence deputy general Su Taiping led troops out by night and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Tibet returned, besieging Long Prefecture; Prefect Han Qingmian and Shence deputy general Su Taiping led troops out by night and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 上謂李泌曰：「每歲諸道貢獻，共直錢五十萬緡，今歲僅得三十萬緡。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Li Bi, "Each year the circuit tributes together are worth five hundred thousand strings of cash; this year we have obtained only three hundred thousand."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Li Bi, "Each year circuit tributes together are worth five hundred thousand strings of cash; this year we have obtained only three hundred thousand."

sentences.zh: 言此誠知失體，然宮中用度殊不足。

translations.literal: To speak of this—I truly know it is beneath imperial dignity, yet palace expenditures are quite insufficient."
translations.idiomatic: To speak of this—I know it is beneath imperial dignity, yet palace expenditures are quite insufficient."

sentences.zh: 」泌曰：「古者天子不私求財，今請歲供宮中錢百萬緡，願陛下不受諸道貢獻及罷宣索。

translations.literal: " Bi said, "In antiquity the Son of Heaven did not seek wealth for himself. I now ask that one million strings be supplied to the palace each year, and I beg Your Majesty not to accept circuit tributes and to abolish requisition orders."
translations.idiomatic: " Bi said, "In antiquity the Son of Heaven did not seek wealth for himself. I now ask that one million strings be supplied to the palace each year, and I beg Your Majesty not to accept circuit tributes and to abolish requisition orders."

sentences.zh: 必有所須，請降敕折稅，不使奸吏因緣誅剝。

translations.literal: If something is needed, issue an edict to levy tax by assessment, and do not let corrupt officials use the occasion to extort and strip the people.
translations.idiomatic: If something is needed, issue an edict to levy tax by assessment, and do not let corrupt officials use the occasion to extort and strip the people.

sentences.zh: 」上從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed this counsel.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor followed this counsel.

sentences.zh: 回紇合骨咄祿可汗屢求和親，且請婚。

translations.literal: The Uighur Qaghan Heluogu repeatedly sought peace through marriage and also requested a marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: The Uighur Qaghan Heluogu repeatedly sought peace through marriage and also requested a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 上未之許。

translations.literal: The emperor had not granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had not granted it.

sentences.zh: 會邊將告乏馬，無以給之，李泌言於上曰：「陛下誠用臣策，數年之後，馬賤於今十倍矣。

translations.literal: It happened that frontier generals reported a shortage of horses and there were none to supply them. Li Bi said to the emperor, "If Your Majesty truly employs my plan, within several years horses will be a tenth of today's price."
translations.idiomatic: Frontier generals reported a shortage of horses and there were none to supply them. Li Bi said to the emperor, "If Your Majesty truly employs my plan, within several years horses will be a tenth of today's price."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「何故？

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "For what reason?"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "For what reason?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「願陛下推至公之心，屈己徇人，為社稷大計，臣乃敢言。

translations.literal: " He replied, "I beg Your Majesty to extend the utmost impartial heart, humble yourself and yield to others for the great plan of the altars of soil and grain—then I dare speak."
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "I beg Your Majesty to extend the utmost impartial heart, humble yourself and yield to others for the great plan of the altars of soil and grain—then I dare speak."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「卿何自疑若是！

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "Why do you doubt yourself so!"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Why do you doubt yourself so!"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣願陛下北和回紇，南通雲南，西結大食、天竺，如此，則吐蕃自困，馬亦易致矣！

translations.literal: " He replied, "I wish Your Majesty to ally with the Uighurs in the north, connect with Yunnan in the south, and join with Dashi and Tianzhu in the west—thus Tibet will constrain itself, and horses will also be easy to obtain!"
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "I wish Your Majesty to ally with the Uighurs in the north, connect with Yunnan in the south, and join with Dashi and Tianzhu in the west—thus Tibet will constrain itself, and horses will also be easy to obtain!"

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「三國當如卿言，至於回紇則不可。

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "The three states should be as you say; as for the Uighurs, it cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "The three states should be as you say; as for the Uighurs, it cannot be done."

sentences.zh: 」泌曰：「臣固知陛下如此，所以不敢早言。

translations.literal: " Bi said, "I knew all along Your Majesty would be thus, which is why I did not dare speak earlier."
translations.idiomatic: " Bi said, "I knew all along Your Majesty would be thus, which is why I did not dare speak earlier."

sentences.zh: 為今之計，當以回紇為先，三國差緩耳。

translations.literal: For the present plan, the Uighurs should come first; the three states can wait a little.
translations.idiomatic: For the present plan, the Uighurs should come first; the three states can wait a little.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「唯回紇卿勿言。

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "Only on the Uighurs—do not speak of it."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Only on the Uighurs—do not speak of it."

sentences.zh: 」泌曰：「臣備位宰相，事有可否在陛下，何至不許臣言！

translations.literal: " Bi said, "I occupy the post of chancellor in name; whether affairs may proceed rests with Your Majesty—how can you not allow me to speak!"
translations.idiomatic: " Bi said, "I occupy the post of chancellor in name; whether affairs may proceed rests with Your Majesty—how can you not allow me to speak!"

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「朕於卿言皆聽之矣，至於和回紇，宜待子孫；

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "In all your other words I heed you; as for making peace with the Uighurs, let that await my descendants;"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "In all your other words I heed you; as for making peace with the Uighurs, let that await my descendants;"

sentences.zh: 於朕之時，則固不可！

translations.literal: in my own lifetime it absolutely cannot be done!"
translations.idiomatic: in my own lifetime it absolutely cannot be done!"

sentences.zh: 」泌曰：「豈非以陝州之恥邪！

translations.literal: " Bi said, "Is it not because of the shame at Shazhou!"
translations.idiomatic: " Bi said, "Is it not because of the shame at Shazhou!"

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「然。

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "It is so."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "It is so."

sentences.zh: 韋少華等以朕之故受辱而死，朕豈能忘之！

translations.literal: Wei Shaohua and others suffered insult and died on my account—how could I forget!"
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shaohua and others suffered insult and died on my account—how could I forget!"

sentences.zh: 屬國家多難，未暇報之，和則決不可。

translations.literal: The realm has been beset with many hardships and I have had no leisure to repay it; peace is absolutely impossible.
translations.idiomatic: The realm has been beset with many hardships and I have had no leisure to repay it; peace is absolutely impossible.

sentences.zh: 卿勿更言！

translations.literal: Do not speak of it again!"
translations.idiomatic: Do not speak of it again!"

sentences.zh: 」泌曰：「害少華者乃牟羽可汗，陛下即位，舉兵入寇，未出其境，今合骨咄祿可汗殺之。

translations.literal: " Bi said, "The one who harmed Shaohua was Qaghan Mouyu. When Your Majesty took the throne he raised troops and invaded; before he had left his own territory the present Qaghan Heluogu killed him."
translations.idiomatic: " Bi said, "The one who harmed Shaohua was Qaghan Mouyu. When Your Majesty took the throne he raised troops and invaded; before he had left his own territory the present Qaghan Heluogu killed him."

sentences.zh: 然則今可汗乃有功於陛下，宜受封賞，又何怨邪！

translations.literal: Thus the present qaghan has rendered merit to Your Majesty and ought to receive enfeoffment and reward—what grievance remains!"
translations.idiomatic: Thus the present qaghan has rendered merit to Your Majesty and ought to receive enfeoffment and reward—what grievance remains!"

sentences.zh: 其後張光晟殺突董等九百餘人，合骨咄祿竟不敢殺朝廷使者，然則合骨咄祿固無罪矣。

translations.literal: Afterward Zhang Guangcheng killed Tudong and more than nine hundred others; Heluogu in the end did not dare kill the court's envoys—thus Heluogu was in fact without guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Zhang Guangcheng killed Tudong and more than nine hundred others; Heluogu in the end did not dare kill the court's envoys—thus Heluogu was in fact without guilt.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「卿以和回紇為是，則朕固非邪？

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "If you hold peace with the Uighurs to be right, then am I in the wrong?"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "If you hold peace with the Uighurs to be right, then am I in the wrong?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣為社稷而言，若苛合取容，何以見肅宗、代宗於天上！

translations.literal: " He replied, "I speak for the altars of soil and grain; if I bent to please and sought only to be accommodated, how could I face Suzong and Daizong in Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "I speak for the altars of soil and grain; if I bent to please and sought only to be accommodated, how could I face Suzong and Daizong in Heaven!"

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「容朕徐思之。

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "Allow me to think on it at leisure."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Give me time to consider this."

sentences.zh: 」自是泌凡十五餘對，未嘗不論回紇事，上終不許。

translations.literal: From then on, in more than fifteen further audiences Bi gave, he never failed to discuss the Uighur affair; the emperor in the end did not grant permission.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, over more than fifteen further audiences, Li Bi never failed to raise the Uighurs—and the emperor still refused in the end.

sentences.zh: 泌曰：「陛下既不許回紇和親，願賜臣骸骨。

translations.literal: Bi said, "Since Your Majesty will not permit marriage alliance with the Uighurs, I beg to be granted my bones."
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi said, "If Your Majesty will not permit alliance with the Uighurs through marriage, I ask leave to resign my post."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「朕非拒諫，但欲與卿較理耳，何至遽欲去朕邪！

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "I am not rejecting remonstrance; I only wished to debate the reasoning with you—how could you so hastily wish to leave me!"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "I am not refusing your counsel—I only wanted to argue the matter through with you. Why would you so quickly want to abandon me!"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「陛下許臣言理，此固天下之福也。

translations.literal: " He replied, "If Your Majesty permits me to discuss reasoning, this is indeed a blessing for the realm."
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "If Your Majesty will hear me out on the merits of the case, that in itself is a blessing for the realm."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「朕不惜屈己與之和，但不能負少華輩。

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "I do not begrudge humbling myself to make peace with them, but I cannot fail men like Shaohua."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "I would not hesitate to humble myself to make peace with them—but I cannot betray men like Shaohua."

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「以臣觀之，少華輩負陛下，非陛下負之也。

translations.literal: " He replied, "As I see it, Shaohua and his associates failed Your Majesty—it was not Your Majesty who failed them."
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "As I see it, Shaohua and his associates failed you—it was not you who failed them."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「何故？

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "For what reason?"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "How so?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「昔回紇葉護將兵助討安慶緒，肅宗但令臣宴勞之於元帥府，先帝未嘗見也。

translations.literal: " He replied, "Formerly when the Uighur Ye Hu led troops to help suppress An Qingxu, Suzong only ordered me to feast and reward him at the marshal's headquarters; the Former Emperor never met him."
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "When the Uighur Ye Hu once led troops to help suppress An Qingxu, Suzong only had me feast and reward him at the marshal's headquarters—the Former Emperor never received him at all."

sentences.zh: 葉護固邀臣至其營，肅宗猶不許。

translations.literal: Ye Hu persistently invited me to his camp, yet Suzong still would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Hu repeatedly pressed me to come to his camp, but Suzong still refused to allow it.

sentences.zh: 及大軍將發，先帝始與相見。

translations.literal: Only when the main army was about to march out did the Former Emperor first meet with him.
translations.idiomatic: Only when the main army was about to set out did the Former Emperor meet him for the first time.

sentences.zh: 所以然者，彼戒狄豺狼也，舉兵入中國之腹，不得不過為之防也。

translations.literal: The reason for this was that they are barbarian wolves; they raised troops into the belly of China—one could not but take excessive precautions against them.
translations.idiomatic: The reason was that they are barbarian wolves who had marched deep into the heart of China—one had no choice but to guard against them to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 陛下在陝，富於春秋，少華輩不能深慮，以萬乘元子徑造其營，又不先與之議相見之儀，使彼得肆其桀驁，豈非少華輩負陛下邪？

translations.literal: When Your Majesty was at Shazhou, rich in youth, Shaohua and his associates could not think deeply; they had the heir of ten thousand chariots go straight to the Uighur camp, and did not first negotiate the protocol for the meeting, allowing the Uighurs to give full vent to their arrogance—is this not Shaohua and his associates failing Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: When you were at Shazhou, still young, Shaohua and his associates failed to think it through: they sent the heir apparent of an empire straight into the Uighur camp without first settling the protocol for the meeting, letting the Uighurs indulge their arrogance—is that not Shaohua and his associates failing you?

sentences.zh: 死不足償責矣。

translations.literal: Death would not suffice to repay the debt.
translations.idiomatic: Death would not be enough to atone for it.

sentences.zh: 且香積之捷，葉護欲引兵入長安，先帝親拜之於馬前以止之，葉護遂不敢入城。

translations.literal: Moreover, after the victory at Xiangji, Ye Hu wished to lead his troops into Chang'an; the Former Emperor personally bowed to him before his horse to stop him, and Ye Hu then did not dare enter the city.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, after the victory at Xiangji, Ye Hu wanted to march his troops into Chang'an; the Former Emperor bowed to him from before his horse to stop him, and Ye Hu then did not dare enter the city.

sentences.zh: 當時觀者十萬餘人，皆歎息曰：『廣平王真華、夷主也！

translations.literal: At the time more than a hundred thousand onlookers all sighed and said, 'The Prince of Guangping is truly a lord of both the Chinese and the barbarians!'
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred thousand onlookers sighed and said, "The Prince of Guangping is truly a ruler for both Chinese and barbarians alike!"

sentences.zh: 』然則先帝所屈者少，所伸者多矣。

translations.literal: ' Thus what the Former Emperor bent on was little, and what he upheld was much.
translations.idiomatic: " Thus what the Former Emperor yielded was little, and what he gained was much.

sentences.zh: 葉護乃牟羽之叔父也。

translations.literal: Ye Hu was Mouyu's uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Hu was Mouyu's uncle.

sentences.zh: 牟羽身為可汗，舉全國之兵赴中原之難，故其志氣驕矜，敢責禮於陛下。

translations.literal: Mouyu, holding the title of qaghan himself, brought all the nation's troops to aid the Central Plains in its distress; hence his spirit was proud and haughty, and he dared demand ceremonial propriety from Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Mouyu held the title of qaghan himself and brought the entire nation's army to relieve the Central Plains in its crisis—so his spirit was proud and overbearing, and he dared demand proper ceremony from Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 陛下天資神武，不為之屈。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, by natural endowment divine and martial, did not bend to him.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, endowed by nature with divine martial prowess, did not yield to him.

sentences.zh: 當是之時，臣不敢言其它，若可汗留陛下於營中，歡飲十日，天下豈得不寒心哉！

translations.literal: At that time I dare not speak of other matters; if the qaghan had detained Your Majesty in camp, feasting joyfully for ten days, would the realm not have had to be chilled at heart!
translations.idiomatic: At that time I dare not speak of anything else—but if the qaghan had kept Your Majesty in camp, feasting for ten days, would the realm not have been chilled with dread!

sentences.zh: 而天威所臨，豺狼馴擾，可汗母捧陛下於貂裘，叱退左右，親送陛下乘馬而歸。

translations.literal: Yet where imperial majesty reached, wolves were tamed to docility; the qaghan's mother lifted Your Majesty in sable furs, shouted down the attendants, and personally saw Your Majesty mount a horse and return.
translations.idiomatic: Yet where imperial majesty reached, even wolves were tamed: the qaghan's mother wrapped Your Majesty in sable furs, shouted down the attendants, and personally saw you mount your horse and ride home.

sentences.zh: 陛下以香積之事觀之，則屈己為是乎？

translations.literal: Your Majesty, viewing the matter of Xiangji—is humbling oneself correct?
translations.idiomatic: Judging by the affair at Xiangji—is humbling oneself the right course?

sentences.zh: 不屈為是乎？

translations.literal: Is not humbling oneself correct?
translations.idiomatic: Or is refusing to humble oneself the right course?

sentences.zh: 陛下屈於牟羽乎？

translations.literal: Did Your Majesty bend to Mouyu?
translations.idiomatic: Did Your Majesty yield to Mouyu?

sentences.zh: 牟羽屈於陛下乎？

translations.literal: Did Mouyu bend to Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: Or did Mouyu yield to Your Majesty?

sentences.zh: 」上謂李晟、馬燧曰：「故舊不宜相逢。

translations.literal: " The emperor said to Li Sheng and Ma Sui, "They say old friends ought not meet again."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said to Li Sheng and Ma Sui, "They say old friends ought not meet again."

sentences.zh: 朕素怨回紇，今聞泌言香積之事，朕自覺少理。

translations.literal: "I have long resented the Uighurs; now, hearing Bi speak of the affair at Xiangji, I feel myself somewhat in the wrong."
translations.idiomatic: "I have long resented the Uighurs, but hearing Li Bi speak of Xiangji, I feel I was partly in the wrong."

sentences.zh: 卿二人以為何如？

translations.literal: "What do you two think?"
translations.idiomatic: "What do you two think?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「果如泌所言，則回紇似可恕。

translations.literal: " They replied, "If it is indeed as Bi says, then the Uighurs seem pardonable."
translations.idiomatic: " They replied, "If it is truly as Li Bi says, then the Uighurs seem forgivable."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「卿二人復不與朕，朕當奈何！

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "You two again will not stand with me—what am I to do!"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "You two again will not side with me—what am I to do!"

sentences.zh: 」泌曰：「臣以為回紇不足怨，曏來宰相乃可怨耳。

translations.literal: " Bi said, "I hold that the Uighurs are not worth resenting; it is the chancellors of recent times who are worth resenting."
translations.idiomatic: " Li Bi said, "I believe the Uighurs are not worth resenting—it is the chancellors of recent times who deserve resentment."

sentences.zh: 今回紇可汗殺牟羽，其國人有再復京城之勳，夫何罪乎！

translations.literal: "The present Uighur qaghan killed Mouyu; his countrymen have the merit of twice recovering the capital—what crime is there!"
translations.idiomatic: "The present Uighur qaghan killed Mouyu, and his people have the merit of twice recovering the capital—what crime have they committed!"

sentences.zh: 吐蕃幸國之災，陷河、隴數千里之地又引兵入京城，使先帝蒙塵於陝，此乃百代必報之仇，況其贊普至今尚存，宰相不為陛下別白言此，乃欲和吐蕃以攻回紇，此為可怨耳。

translations.literal: "Tibet rejoiced in the nation's disaster, seized lands in He and Long stretching thousands of li, and again led troops into the capital, causing the Former Emperor to suffer exile at Shazhou—this is a feud that must be repaid for a hundred generations; moreover the Tibetan tsenpo still lives to this day. The chancellors do not clarify this distinction for Your Majesty, yet wish to make peace with Tibet to attack the Uighurs—this is what is worth resenting."
translations.idiomatic: "Tibet rejoiced in our nation's disaster, seized thousands of li of territory in He and Long, and again marched on the capital, forcing the Former Emperor into exile at Shazhou—this is a feud that must be avenged for generations; moreover the Tibetan tsenpo still lives. The chancellors fail to make this distinction clear for Your Majesty, yet wish to ally with Tibet against the Uighurs—that is what deserves resentment."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「朕與之為怨已久，又聞吐蕃劫盟，今往與之和，得無復拒我，為夷狄之笑乎？

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "I have been at feud with them a long while; moreover I have heard that Tibet violated the alliance by force. If I now go to make peace with them, will they not again reject me and make us the laughingstock of the barbarians?"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "I have been their enemy for years, and I have heard that Tibet broke the alliance by force. If I now seek peace with them, will they not reject me again and make us a laughingstock among the barbarians?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「不然。

translations.literal: " He replied, "Not so."
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "Not at all."

sentences.zh: 臣曩在彭原，今可汗為胡祿都督，與今國相白婆帝皆從聽護而來，臣待之頗親厚，故聞臣為相求和，安有復相拒乎！

translations.literal: "Formerly when I was at Pengyuan, the present qaghan was Hulun regional commander, and the present prime minister Baipodi both came following Ye Hu; I treated them with considerable personal warmth. Thus hearing that I had become chancellor and sought peace, how could they again refuse!"
translations.idiomatic: "When I was at Pengyuan, the present qaghan was Hulun regional commander, and the present prime minister Baipodi both came in Ye Hu's train; I treated them with great personal warmth. When they hear that I have become chancellor and seek peace, how could they refuse again!"

sentences.zh: 臣今請以書與之約：稱臣，為陛下子，每使來不過二百人，印馬不過千匹，無得攜中國人及商胡出塞。

translations.literal: "I now request to write them a letter stipulating: that they call themselves subjects, be Your Majesty's son, that each embassy bring no more than two hundred men, that branded tribute horses number no more than one thousand, and that they may not take Chinese subjects or merchant aliens beyond the frontier."
translations.idiomatic: "I propose to write them a letter setting five terms: they shall call themselves subjects and Your Majesty's son; each embassy shall bring no more than two hundred men; branded tribute horses shall not exceed one thousand; and they may not take Chinese subjects or foreign merchants beyond the frontier."

sentences.zh: 五者皆能如約，則主上必許和親。

translations.literal: "If all five points can be kept as agreed, then the sovereign will surely grant marriage alliance."
translations.idiomatic: "If they can keep all five terms, Your Majesty will surely grant the marriage alliance."

sentences.zh: 如此，威加北荒，旁讋吐蕃，足以快陛下平昔之心矣」上曰：「自至德以來，與為兄弟之國，今一旦欲臣之，彼安肯和乎？

translations.literal: "Thus majesty would be extended over the northern wilds, and Tibet would be awed on the flank—enough to satisfy Your Majesty's long-standing desire." The emperor said, "Since the Zhide era we have been brother-states; now suddenly to wish them to become subjects—will they be willing to make peace?"
translations.idiomatic: "Thus your authority would reach the northern wilds and Tibet would be cowed on the flank—enough to satisfy what Your Majesty has long desired." The emperor said, "Since the Zhide era we have been brother-states; now suddenly to demand that they become subjects—will they agree to peace?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「彼思與中國和親久矣，其可汗、國相素信臣言，若其未諧，但應再發一書耳。

translations.literal: " He replied, "They have long desired marriage alliance with China; their qaghan and prime minister have always trusted my words. If agreement is not reached, one need only send another letter."
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "They have long wanted alliance with China through marriage; their qaghan and prime minister have always trusted my word. If agreement is not reached at once, we need only send another letter."

sentences.zh: 」上從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 既而回紇可汗遣使上表稱兒及臣，凡泌所與約五事，一皆聽命。

translations.literal: Before long the Uighur qaghan dispatched envoys submitting a memorial calling himself son and subject; all five matters Li Bi had stipulated—each was obeyed without exception.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Uighur qaghan sent envoys with a memorial calling himself son and subject; on all five points Li Bi had stipulated, he obeyed without exception.

sentences.zh: 上大喜，謂泌曰：「回紇何畏服卿如此！

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and said to Bi, "How the Uighurs fear and submit to you thus!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and said to Li Bi, "How is it that the Uighurs fear and obey you so completely!"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「此乃陛下威靈，臣何力焉！

translations.literal: " He replied, "This is Your Majesty's awesome authority—what strength had I!"
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "This is Your Majesty's awesome authority—what power had I in the matter!"

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「回紇則既和矣，所以招雲南、大食、天竺奈何！

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "The Uighurs are now reconciled; how then are we to win over Nanzhao, the Arabs, and India?"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "The Uighurs are reconciled—but how are we to win over Nanzhao, the Arabs, and India?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「回紇和，則吐蕃已不敢輕犯塞矣。

translations.literal: " He replied, "With the Uighurs at peace, Tibet already dares not lightly raid the frontier."
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "With the Uighurs at peace, Tibet will no longer dare raid the frontier lightly."

sentences.zh: 次招雲南，則是斷吐蕃之右臂也。

translations.literal: "Next win over Nanzhao—then that severs Tibet's right arm."
translations.idiomatic: "Next win over Nanzhao—that will cut off Tibet's right arm."

sentences.zh: 雲南自漢以臣屬中國，楊國忠無故擾之使叛，臣於吐蕃，苦於吐蕃賦役重，未嘗一日不思復為唐臣也。

translations.literal: "Nanzhao has been China's subject since Han times; Yang Guozhong groundlessly harassed them until they rebelled. They suffer under Tibet's heavy levies and corvée and have not gone a single day without wishing to return as Tang subjects."
translations.idiomatic: "Nanzhao has been China's subject since Han times; Yang Guozhong harassed them without cause until they rebelled. Under Tibet they suffer heavy levies and corvée, and not a day passes without their wishing to return as subjects of Tang."

sentences.zh: 大食在西域為最強，自蔥嶺盡西海，地幾半天下，與天竺皆慕中國，代與吐蕃為仇，臣故知其可招也。

translations.literal: "The Arabs are strongest in the Western Regions; from the Pamirs to the western sea their lands are nearly half the world. Both they and India admire China and have generation after generation been enemies of Tibet—I therefore know they can be won over."
translations.idiomatic: "The Arabs are the strongest power in the Western Regions; from the Pamirs to the western sea their lands cover nearly half the world. Both they and India admire China and have been enemies of Tibet for generations—I therefore know they can be won over."

sentences.zh: 」癸亥，遣回紇使者合闕將軍歸，許以咸安公主妻可汗，歸其馬價絹五萬匹。

translations.literal: " On the guihai day, the court sent the Uighur envoy General Heque back, promising Princess Xian'an in marriage to the qaghan and returning horse-price silk of fifty thousand bolts.
translations.idiomatic: On the guihai day, the court sent the Uighur envoy General Heque home, promising Princess Xian'an in marriage to the qaghan and returning fifty thousand bolts of silk as payment for horses.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃寇華亭及連雲堡，皆陷之。

translations.literal: Tibet raided Huating and Lianyun Fortress; both fell.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet attacked Huating and Lianyun Fortress; both were taken.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，吐蕃驅二城之民數千人及邠、涇人畜萬計而去，置之彈箏峽西。

translations.literal: On the jiaxu day, Tibet drove off several thousand civilians from the two cities and tens of thousands of people and livestock from Bin and Jing, taking them west of Danzheng Gorge.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiaxu day, Tibet drove off several thousand civilians from the two cities and tens of thousands of people and livestock from Bin and Jing, resettling them west of Danzheng Gorge.

sentences.zh: 涇州恃連雲為斥候，連雲既陷，西門不開，門外皆為虜境，樵采路絕。

translations.literal: Jing Prefecture relied on Lianyun as its outpost scout; once Lianyun fell, the west gate was not opened, and outside the gate all was enemy territory—the paths for fuel and foraging were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Prefecture had relied on Lianyun as its forward outpost; once Lianyun fell, the west gate stayed shut and everything beyond it was enemy territory—the routes for firewood and foraging were cut off.

sentences.zh: 每收穫，必陳兵以扞之，多失時，得空穗而已。

translations.literal: Each harvest had to be guarded by deployed troops; much time was lost, and they got only empty husks.
translations.idiomatic: Each harvest had to be protected by deployed troops; much time was lost, and they harvested only empty husks.

sentences.zh: 由是涇州常苦乏食。

translations.literal: Hence Jing Prefecture was constantly afflicted by food shortages.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Jing Prefecture was chronically short of food.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲申，吐蕃寇豐義城，前鋒至大回原，邠寧節度使韓游瑰擊卻之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the jiashen day, Tibet raided Fengyi City; the vanguard reached Dayuan Plain, and Bining military commissioner Han Yougui repulsed them.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the jiashen day, Tibet attacked Fengyi City; the vanguard reached Dayuan Plain, and Bining military commissioner Han Yougui drove them back.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，復寇長武城，又城故原州而屯之。

translations.literal: On the yiyou day, they again raided Changwu City, and also fortified old Yuan Prefecture and garrisoned it.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiyou day, they attacked Changwu City again, and also rebuilt and garrisoned old Yuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 妖僧李軟奴自言：「本皇族，見岳、瀆神命己為天子。

translations.literal: The sorcerer-monk Li Ruanu declared of himself, "By origin I am of the imperial clan; the gods of the mountains and rivers commanded me to be Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The sorcerer-monk Li Ruanu declared, "I am of the imperial clan by birth; the gods of the mountains and rivers have commanded me to be Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 」結殿前射生將韓欽緒等謀作亂。

translations.literal: " He joined with Palace Corps bowman-captain Han Qinxu and others in plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: " He joined Palace Corps bowman-captain Han Qinxu and others in plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，其黨告之，上命捕送內侍省推之。

translations.literal: On the bingxu day, his faction informed on them; the emperor ordered them seized and sent to the Inner Palace Service for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingxu day, members of the plot informed on them; the emperor ordered them arrested and sent to the Inner Palace Service for interrogation.

sentences.zh: 李晟聞之，遽僕於地曰：「晟族滅矣！

translations.literal: When Li Sheng heard of it, he suddenly threw himself on the ground and said, "Sheng's clan is destroyed!"
translations.idiomatic: When Li Sheng heard of it, he suddenly threw himself to the ground and cried, "My clan is ruined!"

sentences.zh: 」李泌問其故，晟曰：「晟新罹謗毀，中外有家人千餘，若有一人在其黨中，則兄亦不能救矣。

translations.literal: " Li Bi asked the reason; Sheng said, "Sheng has newly suffered slander; inside and outside I have more than a thousand family members—if even one person is in their faction, then my elder brother too cannot be saved."
translations.idiomatic: " Li Bi asked why; Li Sheng said, "I have just been slandered; I have more than a thousand kinsmen inside and outside the court—if even one of them is in their faction, not even my elder brother can save me."

sentences.zh: 」泌乃奏：「大獄一起，所連引必多，外間人情心兇懼，請出付台推。

translations.literal: " Bi then memorialized: "When a great case is opened, those implicated by extension are always many; among the people outside, hearts are fierce with fear. I request that the matter be handed over to the Censorate for investigation."
translations.idiomatic: " Li Bi then memorialized: "When a major case is opened, those implicated are always many; outside the court people are gripped with fear. I ask that the case be transferred to the Censorate for investigation."

sentences.zh: 」上從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 欽緒，游瑰之子也，亡抵邠州。

translations.literal: Qinxu was Yougui's son; he fled and reached Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Qinxu was Han Yougui's son; he fled and reached Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 游瑰出屯長武城，留後械送京師。

translations.literal: Yougui, having gone out to encamp at Changwu City, had the acting prefect send him in fetters to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui, who had gone out to encamp at Changwu City, had the acting prefect send him to the capital in chains.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，腰斬欽奴等八人，北軍之士坐死者八百餘人，而朝廷之臣無連及者。

translations.literal: On the renchen day, Qinnu and eight others were executed at the waist; more than eight hundred northern army soldiers were put to death for complicity, yet no court ministers were implicated.
translations.idiomatic: On the renchen day, Qinnu and eight others were cut in two at the waist; more than eight hundred northern army soldiers were executed for complicity, but no court ministers were implicated.

sentences.zh: 韓游瑰委軍詣闕謝，上遣使止之，委任如初。

translations.literal: Han Yougui relinquished command and came to the palace to apologize; the emperor sent messengers to stop him, and his trust and appointment remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yougui relinquished his command and came to court to apologize; the emperor sent messengers to stop him, and his trust and appointment remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 游瑰又械送欽緒二子，上亦宥之。

translations.literal: Yougui also sent Qinxu's two sons in fetters; the emperor pardoned them as well.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui also sent Qinxu's two sons to the capital in chains; the emperor pardoned them as well.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃以苦寒不入寇，而糧運不繼。

translations.literal: Tibet, because of bitter cold, did not raid; yet grain transport could not keep up.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet did not raid because of the bitter cold, but grain supplies could not keep up.

sentences.zh: 十一月，詔渾瑊歸河中，李元諒歸華州，劉昌分其眾五千歸汴州，自餘防秋兵退屯鳳翔、京兆諸縣以就食。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, an edict ordered Hun Jian to return to Hezhong, Li Yuanliang to return to Hua Prefecture, Liu Chang to take five thousand of the troops back to Bian Prefecture; the remaining frontier-defense soldiers withdrew to garrison Fengxiang, Jingzhao, and other counties to draw rations locally.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, an edict ordered Hun Jian back to Hezhong, Li Yuanliang back to Hua Prefecture, and Liu Chang to take five thousand troops back to Bian Prefecture; the remaining autumn-defense troops withdrew to Fengxiang, Jingzhao, and other counties to live off local supplies.

sentences.zh: 十二月，韓游瑰入朝。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Han Yougui entered court audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Han Yougui came to court for audience.

sentences.zh: 自興元以來，至是歲最為豐稔，米斗直錢百五十、粟八十，詔所在和糴。

translations.literal: From Xingyuan until this year, the harvest was the most abundant; rice per dou cost a hundred fifty cash and millet eighty; an edict ordered equal-purchase requisitioning everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: From Xingyuan until this year, the harvest was the most abundant yet; rice sold for a hundred fifty cash per dou and millet for eighty; an edict ordered government grain purchases throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，上畋於新店，入民趙光奇家，問：「百姓樂乎？

translations.literal: On the gengchen day, the emperor hunted at Xindian, entered the home of the commoner Zhao Guangqi, and asked, "Are the common people happy?"
translations.idiomatic: On the gengchen day, the emperor hunted at Xindian, entered the home of a commoner named Zhao Guangqi, and asked, "Are the people happy?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「不樂。

translations.literal: " He replied, "Not happy."
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "No, they are not."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「今歲頗稔，何為不樂？

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "This year the harvest has been quite abundant—why not happy?"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "This year the harvest has been quite good—why are they not happy?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「詔令不信。

translations.literal: " He replied, "Edicts are not trusted."
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "Imperial edicts are not trusted."

sentences.zh: 前雲兩稅之外悉無它徭，今非稅而誅求者殆過於稅。

translations.literal: "Previously it was declared that apart from the two taxes there would be no other corvée; now extractions that are not taxes almost exceed the taxes themselves."
translations.idiomatic: "It was declared before that apart from the two taxes there would be no other levies—yet extractions that are not taxes now almost exceed the taxes themselves."

sentences.zh: 後又云和糴，而實強取之，曾不識一錢。

translations.literal: "Later it was declared equal-purchase requisitioning, but in fact grain was seized by force—not a single coin was ever seen."
translations.idiomatic: "Later it was called government purchase of grain, but in fact grain was seized by force—not a single coin was ever paid."

sentences.zh: 始雲所糴粟麥納於道次，今則遣致京西行營，動數百里，車摧牛斃，破產不能支。

translations.literal: "At first it was said the grain and wheat purchased would be delivered at roadside stations; now they are sent to the western expeditionary camp in the capital region, often several hundred li—carts break, oxen drop dead, and families are ruined beyond bearing."
translations.idiomatic: "At first it was said purchased grain would be delivered at roadside stations; now it must be sent to the western expeditionary camp near the capital, often hundreds of li away—carts break down, oxen die, and families are ruined trying to comply."

sentences.zh: 愁苦如此，何樂之有！

translations.literal: "With bitterness and distress such as this, what happiness could there be!"
translations.idiomatic: "With misery like this, what happiness could there be!"

sentences.zh: 每有詔書優恤，徒空文耳！

translations.literal: "Whenever edicts come down with gracious relief, they are empty words only!"
translations.idiomatic: "Whenever edicts come down promising relief, they are nothing but empty words!"

sentences.zh: 恐聖主深居九重，皆未知之也！

translations.literal: "I fear the sage sovereign, deep within the ninefold palace, knows none of this!"
translations.idiomatic: "I fear the sage sovereign, deep within the palace, knows nothing of this!"

sentences.zh: 」上命復其家。

translations.literal: " The emperor ordered his household restored.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ordered Zhao Guangqi's household tax obligations restored.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：甚矣唐德宗之難寤也！

translations.literal: Master Guang commented: How hard it is for Tang Dezong to awaken!
translations.idiomatic: Master Guang commented: How deeply Tang Dezong fails to awaken!

sentences.zh: 自古所患者，人君之澤壅而不下達，小民之情郁而不上通；

translations.literal: From antiquity what has been feared is that the sovereign's favor becomes blocked and does not reach below, while the common people's feelings are pent up and do not reach above;
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity the great fear has been that the sovereign's grace is blocked and never reaches the people below, while the common people's grievances are pent up and never reach the ruler above;

sentences.zh: 故君勤恤於上而民不懷，民愁怨於下而君不知，以至於離叛危亡，凡以此也。

translations.literal: thus though the ruler is diligent in care above the people do not reciprocate, and though the people groan in resentment below the ruler does not know—leading to separation, rebellion, and perilous ruin; all stem from this.
translations.idiomatic: thus though the ruler is diligent in care above, the people below do not respond in kind; though the people groan in resentment below, the ruler above does not know—leading to separation, rebellion, and ruin. All of this stems from that blockage.

sentences.zh: 德宗幸以游獵得至民家，值光奇敢言而知民疾苦，此乃千載之遇也。

translations.literal: Dezong happened through the hunt to reach a commoner's home, and encountered Guangqi who dared speak frankly and learn the people's hardships—this was a meeting of once in a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong happened through a hunting excursion to reach a commoner's home and met Guangqi, who dared speak frankly and reveal the people's hardships—this was a once-in-a-thousand-years opportunity.

sentences.zh: 固當按有司之廢格詔書，殘虐下民，橫增賦斂，盜匿公財，及左右諂諛日稱民間豐樂者而誅之。

translations.literal: He should at once investigate officials who had shelved and blocked edicts, cruelly abused the lower people, wantonly increased levies, and embezzled public funds, along with those at court who fawned and daily proclaimed the people's abundance and joy—and put them to death.
translations.idiomatic: He should have at once investigated officials who shelved edicts, cruelly abused the common people, wantonly increased levies, and embezzled public funds, along with courtiers who fawned on him and daily proclaimed the people's prosperity—and put them to death.

sentences.zh: 然後洗心易慮，一新其政，屏浮飾，廢虛文，謹號令，敦誠信，察真偽，辨忠邪，矜困窮，伸冤滯，則太平之業可致矣。

translations.literal: Only then wash the heart and change thought, renew policy entirely, set aside superficial display, abolish empty documents, be strict in commands, encourage good faith, examine truth and falsehood, distinguish loyal from treacherous, take pity on the distressed and poor, and redress wrongs long pent up—then the enterprise of great peace could be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Only then should he have purged his heart of old habits, renewed his policies entirely, set aside superficial display, abolish empty formalities, enforce commands strictly, cultivate good faith, distinguish truth from falsehood, loyal from treacherous, show compassion for the poor and distressed, and redress long-standing wrongs—then the enterprise of great peace could have been achieved.

sentences.zh: 釋此不為，乃復光奇之家。

translations.literal: Relinquishing this and not doing it, he merely restored Guangqi's household.
translations.idiomatic: Instead of doing any of this, he merely restored Guangqi's household tax obligations.

sentences.zh: 夫以四海之廣，兆民之眾，又安得人人自言於天子而戶戶復其徭賦乎！

translations.literal: For a realm as vast as the four seas and a populace as numerous as the myriad millions—how could every person speak to the Son of Heaven himself, and every household have its corvée and levies restored!
translations.idiomatic: For a realm as vast as the four seas and a populace numbering in the millions—how could every person speak directly to the Son of Heaven, and every household have its levies restored!

sentences.zh: 李泌以李軟奴之黨猶有在北軍未發者，請大郝以安之。

translations.literal: Li Bi, because among Li Ruanu's faction there were still men in the northern army who had not yet acted, requested a general amnesty to reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi, knowing that some of Li Ruanu's accomplices in the northern army had not yet acted, requested a general amnesty to reassure them.

sentences.zh: 德宗神武聖文皇帝八貞元四年（

translations.literal: The Divine Martial Sage Literary Emperor Dezong, Zhenyuan year four (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong, the Divine Martial and Sage Literary Emperor—Zhenyuan year 4 (

sentences.zh: 戊辰，公元七八八年）

translations.literal: wuchen, CE 788)
translations.idiomatic: wuchen, AD 788)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，庚戌朔，赦天下，詔兩稅等第，自今三年一定。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the gengxu new moon, a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm; an edict fixed ranks for the two taxes, to be adjusted once every three years from now on.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the gengxu new moon, a general amnesty was proclaimed; an edict fixed tax brackets for the two-tax system, to be reassessed every three years from this point forward.

sentences.zh: 李泌奏京官俸太薄，請自三師以下悉倍其俸。

translations.literal: Li Bi memorialized that the salaries of capital officials were too thin and requested that from the Three Preceptors downward all salaries be doubled.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi memorialized that the salaries of capital officials were too low and requested that salaries be doubled for all ranks from the Three Preceptors downward.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 壬申，以宣武行營節度使劉昌為涇原節度使。

translations.literal: On the renshen day, Xuanwu expeditionary military commissioner Liu Chang was appointed military commissioner of Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On the renshen day, Liu Chang, expeditionary military commissioner of Xuanwu, was appointed military commissioner of Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，以鎮國節度使李元諒為隴右節度使。

translations.literal: On the jiaxu day, Zhenguo military commissioner Li Yuanliang was appointed Longyou military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiaxu day, Li Yuanliang, military commissioner of Zhenguo, was appointed military commissioner of Longyou.

sentences.zh: 昌、元諒，皆帥卒力田，數年，軍食充羨，涇、隴稍安。

translations.literal: Liu Chang and Li Yuanliang both led their troops in farming; within several years military provisions were abundant, and Jing and Long grew somewhat secure.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chang and Li Yuanliang both had their soldiers farm the land; within a few years army rations were plentiful, and the Jing and Long regions grew somewhat stable.

sentences.zh: 韓游瑰之入朝也，軍中以為必不返，餞送甚薄。

translations.literal: When Han Yougui went to court, the army believed he would certainly not return, and their farewell send-off was very meager.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Yougui went to the capital, the troops assumed he would never come back, and they gave him a very stingy farewell.

sentences.zh: 游環見上，盛陳築豐義城可以制吐蕃；

translations.literal: Yougui saw the emperor and at length argued that building Fengyi Fort could restrain the Tibetans.
translations.idiomatic: When Yougui met the emperor, he spoke at length about how building Fengyi Fort could check the Tibetans.

sentences.zh: 上悅，遣還鎮。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and sent him back to his command.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and sent him back to his post.

sentences.zh: 軍中憂懼者眾，游環忌都虞候虞鄉范希朝有功名，得眾心，求其罪，將殺之。

translations.literal: Many in the army were anxious and afraid; Yougui envied chief adjutant Fan Xichao of Yuxiang for his achievements and reputation and for winning the troops' hearts, sought grounds for a charge against him, and was about to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Many in the army were anxious and afraid. Yougui resented chief adjutant Fan Xichao of Yuxiang, who had distinguished himself, won the soldiers' loyalty, and enjoyed a strong reputation; he hunted for a pretext to kill him.

sentences.zh: 希朝奔鳳翔，上召之，置於左神策軍。

translations.literal: Xichao fled to Fengxiang; the emperor summoned him and placed him in the Left Shence Army.
translations.idiomatic: Xichao fled to Fengxiang. The emperor summoned him and assigned him to the Left Shence Army.

sentences.zh: 游環帥眾築豐義城，二版而潰。

translations.literal: Yougui led the masses to build Fengyi Fort; after two courses of wall it collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui led his troops to build Fengyi Fort, but after two sections of wall were raised it collapsed.

sentences.zh: 二月，元友直運淮南錢帛二十萬至長安，李泌悉輸之大盈庫。

translations.literal: In the second month, Yuan Youzhi transported two hundred thousand in cash and silk goods from Huainan to Chang'an, and Li Bi had it all delivered to the Daying Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Yuan Youzhi brought two hundred thousand in cash and silk from Huainan to Chang'an, and Li Bi had all of it deposited in the Daying Treasury.

sentences.zh: 然上猶數有宣索，乃敕諸道勿令宰相知。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor still repeatedly issued requisitions, and then ordered the various circuits not to let the chief ministers know.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor still made repeated requisitions, and ordered the various circuits not to inform the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 泌聞之，惆悵而不敢言。

translations.literal: When Bi heard of it, he was distressed but did not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: When Bi heard of this, he was deeply troubled but did not dare say anything.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：王者以天下為家，天下之財皆其有也。

translations.literal: Master Guang commented: A king takes all under Heaven as his home, and all the wealth of the realm is his.
translations.idiomatic: Master Guang commented: A true king treats the realm as his household, and all its wealth belongs to him.

sentences.zh: 阜天下之財以養天下之民，己必豫焉。

translations.literal: He amasses the wealth of the realm to nourish the people of the realm, and he himself must surely share in it.
translations.idiomatic: He gathers the realm's wealth to sustain its people—and he himself must surely share in that abundance.

sentences.zh: 或乃更為私藏，此匹夫之鄙志也。

translations.literal: To turn it instead into a private hoard—this is the base mind of a common man.
translations.idiomatic: To hoard it instead as private treasure is the petty impulse of an ordinary man.

sentences.zh: 古人有言曰：貧不學儉。

translations.literal: The ancients had a saying: "The poor need not learn thrift."
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said, "The poor need not be taught thrift."

sentences.zh: 夫多財者，奢欲之所自來也。

translations.literal: For where wealth is abundant, extravagant desires arise of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Great wealth is the very source from which extravagant desires spring.

sentences.zh: 李泌欲弭德宗之欲而豐其私財，財豐則欲滋矣。

translations.literal: Li Bi wished to quell Dezong's desires yet enrich his private treasury; when wealth grows rich, desires grow stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi sought to restrain Dezong's appetites while swelling his private coffers—but the richer the treasury, the stronger the desires become.

sentences.zh: 財不稱欲，能無求乎！

translations.literal: When wealth does not match desire, how can there fail to be demands!
translations.idiomatic: When wealth cannot satisfy desire, how can demands fail to follow!

sentences.zh: 是猶啟其門而禁其出也！

translations.literal: This is like opening the door yet forbidding anyone to go out!
translations.idiomatic: That is like opening a door and then forbidding anyone to pass through!

sentences.zh: 雖德宗之多僻，亦泌所以相之者非其道故也。

translations.literal: Although Dezong had many eccentric ways, it was also because the way in which Bi served as his minister was not the right path.
translations.idiomatic: Though Dezong had many eccentric ways, Bi also failed as his minister because he pursued the wrong course.

sentences.zh: 咸陽人或上言：「臣見白起，令臣奏云：『請為國家幹御西陲。

translations.literal: A man of Xianyang submitted a memorial: "I saw Bai Qi, and he ordered me to report: 'I ask to defend the western frontier for the state.
translations.idiomatic: A man from Xianyang submitted a memorial: "I saw Bai Qi, and he told me to report: 'I wish to defend the western frontier for the state.

sentences.zh: 正月，吐蕃必大下，當為朝廷破之以取信。

translations.literal: In the first month the Tibetans will surely come down in force; I shall break them for the court to win trust.'"
translations.idiomatic: In the first month the Tibetans will surely invade in force; I shall defeat them for the court and thereby win your trust.'"

sentences.zh: 』」既而吐蕃入寇，邊將敗之，不能深入。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the Tibetans invaded; border generals defeated them, and they could not penetrate deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Tibetans did invade, but border generals defeated them and kept them from penetrating deep into Tang territory.

sentences.zh: 上以為信然，欲於京城立廟，贈司徒，李泌曰：「臣聞『國將興，聽於人。

translations.literal: The emperor believed it was true and wished to erect a temple in the capital and posthumously grant him the rank of Situ; Li Bi said, "Your servant has heard, 'When a state is about to rise, it heeds men.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took this as proof and wanted to build a temple in the capital and posthumously grant Bai Qi the rank of Situ. Li Bi said, "I have heard that 'when a state is about to flourish, it listens to men.'

sentences.zh: 』今將帥立功而陛下褒賞白起，臣恐邊臣解體矣！

translations.literal: Now generals have achieved merit, yet Your Majesty would honor and reward Bai Qi—I fear the border officials will lose heart!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet now living generals have won victories while Your Majesty would honor Bai Qi instead—I fear the border commanders will lose heart!"

sentences.zh: 若立廟京城，盛為祈禱，流聞四方，將長巫風。

translations.literal: If a temple is built in the capital and grand prayers are offered, and this spreads to the four quarters, it will foster shamanistic ways.
translations.idiomatic: If a temple is built in the capital and grand prayers are offered there, word will spread everywhere and encourage shamanistic practices.

sentences.zh: 今杜郵有舊祠，請敕府縣葺之，則不至驚人耳目矣。

translations.literal: At present there is an old shrine at Duyou; I ask that the prefecture and county be ordered to repair it—then it will not startle people's eyes and ears.
translations.idiomatic: There is already an old shrine at Duyou; please order the local officials to repair it. That would not draw undue attention.

sentences.zh: 且白起列國之將，贈三公太重，請贈兵部尚書可矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, Bai Qi was a general of the Warring States; to grant the Three Excellencies would be too great—I ask that Minister of War suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Bai Qi was merely a general of the Warring States period; granting him one of the Three Excellencies would be excessive. Minister of War would be enough.

sentences.zh: 」上笑曰：「卿於白起亦惜官乎！

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and said, "Are you also stingy with rank on Bai Qi's account!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said, "So even you begrudge Bai Qi an honorary title!"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「人神一也。

translations.literal: He replied, "Men and spirits are one.
translations.idiomatic: Bi replied, "Men and spirits are alike in this.

sentences.zh: 陛下倘不之惜，則神亦不以為榮矣。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not begrudge it, then the spirit too will not regard it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty does not value the title, then the spirit will not regard it as an honor either.

sentences.zh: 」上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 泌自陳衰老，獨任宰相，精力耗竭，既未聽其去，乞更除一相。

translations.literal: Bi declared himself aged; serving alone as chief minister, his strength was exhausted; since the emperor would not allow him to leave, he begged that another chief minister be appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Bi said he was growing old; serving as the sole chief minister had exhausted him, and since the emperor would not let him retire, he asked that another chief minister be appointed.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕深知卿勞苦，但未得其人耳。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I fully know your toil, but I have not yet found the right man."
