translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I know full well how hard you have worked, but I have not yet found the right person."

sentences.zh: 」上從容與泌論即位以來宰相，曰：「盧杞忠清強介，人言杞奸邪，朕殊不覺其然。

translations.literal: At leisure the emperor discussed with Bi the chief ministers since his accession and said, "Lu Qi is loyal, pure, strong, and upright; people say Qi is treacherous and wicked, but I do not feel that at all."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then spoke at ease with Bi about the chief ministers since his accession. He said, "Lu Qi is loyal, upright, firm, and principled. People call him treacherous and wicked, but I do not see it that way at all."

sentences.zh: 」泌曰：「人言杞奸邪而陛下獨不覺其奸邪，此乃杞之所以為奸邪也。

translations.literal: Bi said, "People say Qi is treacherous and wicked, yet Your Majesty alone does not perceive his treachery and wickedness—this is precisely why Qi is treacherous and wicked.
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "People say Lu Qi is treacherous and wicked, yet Your Majesty alone fails to see his treachery—that is precisely what makes him treacherous and wicked.

sentences.zh: 倘陛下覺之，豈有建中之亂乎！

translations.literal: Had Your Majesty perceived it, would there have been the Jianzhong turmoil!"
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty had seen it, would there ever have been the Jianzhong rebellion!"

sentences.zh: 杞以私隙殺楊炎，擠顏真卿於死地，激李懷光使叛，賴陛下聖明竄逐之，人心頓喜，天亦悔禍。

translations.literal: Qi killed Yang Yan over a private grudge, drove Yan Zhenqing to his death, and provoked Li Huaiguang into rebellion; thanks to Your Majesty's sagacity in banishing him, people's hearts were instantly gladdened and Heaven too repented the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi killed Yang Yan over a private grudge, hounded Yan Zhenqing to his death, and provoked Li Huaiguang into rebellion. Thanks to Your Majesty's wisdom in banishing him, the people rejoiced at once and Heaven itself seemed to repent the disaster.

sentences.zh: 不然，亂何由弭！

translations.literal: Otherwise, how could the turmoil have been quelled!"
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, how could the rebellion ever have been ended!"

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「楊炎以童子視朕，每論事，朕可其奏則悅，與之往復問難，即怒而辭位，觀其意以朕為不足與言故也。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Yang Yan treated me like a child; whenever we discussed affairs, if I approved his memorial he was pleased, but if I questioned him back and forth he grew angry and offered to resign—judging by his attitude, he thought me unworthy to speak with."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Yang Yan treated me like a child. Whenever we discussed policy, he was pleased if I approved his memorial, but if I pressed him with questions he grew angry and threatened to resign. From his manner, he clearly thought me unworthy of real conversation."

sentences.zh: 以是交不可忍，非由杞也。

translations.literal: For that reason the association was unbearable; it was not because of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I could not tolerate working with him—it had nothing to do with Lu Qi.

sentences.zh: 建中之亂，術士豫請城奉天，此蓋天命，非杞所能致也！

translations.literal: The Jianzhong turmoil—a diviner beforehand urged fortifying Fengtian; this was surely Heaven's decree, not something Qi could have brought about!"
translations.idiomatic: As for the Jianzhong rebellion, a diviner had beforehand urged fortifying Fengtian—that was Heaven's decree, not something Lu Qi could have caused!"

sentences.zh: 」泌曰：「天命，他人皆可以言之，惟君相不可言。

translations.literal: Bi said, "Heaven's decree—others may all speak of it, but only the ruler and his minister may not.
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "Others may speak of Heaven's decree, but the ruler and his minister must not.

sentences.zh: 蓋君相所以造命也。

translations.literal: For it is the ruler and minister who shape destiny.
translations.idiomatic: It is the ruler and his minister who shape destiny.

sentences.zh: 若言命，則禮樂刑政皆無所用矣。

translations.literal: If one speaks of fate, then rites, music, punishments, and government are all of no use.
translations.idiomatic: If one appeals to fate, then rites, music, law, and government all become useless.

sentences.zh: 紂曰：『我生不有命在天！

translations.literal: King Zhou said, 'My life—does it not have its mandate in Heaven!'
translations.idiomatic: King Zhou of Shang said, 'My life is ordained by Heaven!'

sentences.zh: 』此商之所以亡也！

translations.literal: This is why Shang perished!"
translations.idiomatic: That is why the Shang dynasty fell!"

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「朕好與人較量理體：崔祐甫性褊躁，朕難之，則應對失次，朕常知其短而護之。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I like to debate principles with others: Cui Youfu was narrow and impetuous by nature; when I pressed him, his replies lost order—I often knew his faults yet protected him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I like to debate principles with my ministers. Cui Youfu was narrow-minded and impetuous; when I pressed him hard, he lost his composure. I often knew his weaknesses yet shielded him.

sentences.zh: 楊炎論事亦有可采，而氣色粗傲，難之輒勃然怒，無復君臣之禮，所以每見令人忿發。

translations.literal: Yang Yan's policy discussions also had points worth taking, but his bearing was coarse and arrogant; when pressed he would flare up in anger, with no further observance of the rites between ruler and minister—therefore every audience made one burn with indignation.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan's policy arguments often had merit, but his manner was coarse and arrogant. When challenged he would flare up in anger and forget the rites between ruler and minister. Every audience with him left me furious.

sentences.zh: 餘人則不敢復言。

translations.literal: The rest then did not dare speak again.
translations.idiomatic: After that, the others did not dare speak up again.

sentences.zh: 盧杞小心，朕所言無不從。

translations.literal: Lu Qi was cautious; whatever I said, he never failed to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi was deferential; he never failed to do whatever I said.

sentences.zh: 又無學，不能與朕往復，故朕所懷常不盡也。

translations.literal: Moreover he had no learning and could not debate back and forth with me, so what I kept in mind was often not fully expressed.
translations.idiomatic: But he had no learning and could not debate with me, so I could never fully express what was on my mind.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「杞言無不從，豈忠臣乎！

translations.literal: He replied, "Qi never failed to follow your words—is that a loyal minister!
translations.idiomatic: Bi replied, "Lu Qi never contradicted you—is that what a loyal minister does!

sentences.zh: 夫『言而莫予違』，此孔子所謂『一言喪邦』者也！

translations.literal: For 'words to which none may say no'—this is what Confucius called 'one word and the state is lost'!"
translations.idiomatic: For 'words to which no one may object'—that is what Confucius meant by 'one word can destroy a state'!"

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「惟卿則異彼三人者。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Only you differ from those three.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Only you are different from those three.

sentences.zh: 朕言當，卿有喜色；

translations.literal: When my words were right, you showed joy;
translations.idiomatic: When I spoke rightly, you looked pleased;

sentences.zh: 不當，常有憂色。

translations.literal: when they were not right, you often showed concern.
translations.idiomatic: when I was wrong, you often looked troubled.

sentences.zh: 雖時有逆耳之言，如曏來紂及喪邦之類。

translations.literal: Although at times there were words hard to hear, like just now about King Zhou and the loss of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Even when you spoke harsh truths, as you just did about King Zhou and the fall of a state,

sentences.zh: 朕細思之，皆卿先事而言，如此則理安，如彼則危亂，言雖深切而氣色和順，無楊炎之陵傲。

translations.literal: When I ponder it closely, you always speak beforehand of events: thus there is order and peace, otherwise danger and turmoil; though your words are deeply cutting, your bearing is harmonious, without Yang Yan's overbearing arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: on reflection I see that you always speak before events unfold: follow your counsel and order prevails; ignore it and disaster follows. Your words may cut deep, yet your manner stays calm—nothing like Yang Yan's overbearing arrogance.

sentences.zh: 朕問難往復，卿辭理不屈，又無好勝之志，直使朕中懷已盡屈服而不能不從，此朕新以私喜於得卿也。

translations.literal: When I questioned and debated back and forth, your reasoning did not yield, yet you had no desire to prevail; you simply made what was in my heart fully expressed until I yielded and could not but follow—this is why I am privately delighted anew at having you.
translations.idiomatic: When I pressed you in debate, your reasoning never broke, yet you had no desire to win. You simply drew out everything in my heart until I had no choice but to agree. That is why I am privately overjoyed to have you.

sentences.zh: 」泌曰：「陛下能用相尚多，今皆不論，何也？

translations.literal: Bi said, "Your Majesty has been able to use many chief ministers; why discuss none of them now?"
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "Your Majesty has appointed many chief ministers—why discuss none of the others?"

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「彼皆非所謂相也。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "None of them were what I call chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "None of them were true chief ministers, in my view.

sentences.zh: 凡相者，必委以政事，如玄宗時牛仙客、陳希烈，可以謂之相乎！

translations.literal: In general a chief minister must be entrusted with state affairs—like Niu Xianke and Chen Xilie in Xuanzong's time; can they be called chief ministers!
translations.idiomatic: A true chief minister must be entrusted with governing the state. Take Niu Xianke and Chen Xilie under Xuanzong—can they be called chief ministers!

sentences.zh: 如肅宗、代宗之任卿，雖不受其名，乃真相耳。

translations.literal: As when Suzong and Daizong employed you—though you did not receive the title, you were truly a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong and Daizong employed you, you did not hold the title, yet you were a true chief minister.

sentences.zh: 必以官至平章事為相，則王武俊之徒皆相也。

translations.literal: If one must hold the office of Grand Councilor to be a chief minister, then Wang Wujun and his like are all chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: If holding the title of Grand Councilor alone makes one a chief minister, then Wang Wujun and men like him would all count as chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 」劉昌復築連雲堡。

translations.literal: Liu Chang again built Lianyun Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chang rebuilt Lianyun Fort.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，乙未，更命殿前左、右射生曰神威軍，與左、右羽林、龍武、神武、神策號曰十軍。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, on the yimwei day, the Left and Right She-sheng of the Palace Guard were renamed the Shenwei Army; together with the Left and Right Yulin, Longwu, Shenwu, and Shence they were called the Ten Armies.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on the yimwei day, the Left and Right She-sheng units of the Palace Guard were renamed the Shenwei Army. Together with the Left and Right Yulin, Longwu, Shenwu, and Shence armies, they were called the Ten Armies.

sentences.zh: 神策尤盛，多戍京西，散屯畿甸。

translations.literal: The Shence was especially powerful, garrisoning much of the western capital region and scattered across the capital districts.
translations.idiomatic: The Shence Army was especially powerful, with many troops garrisoned west of the capital and detachments scattered across the capital region.

sentences.zh: 福建觀察使吳詵，輕其軍士脆弱，苦役之。

translations.literal: Fujian observation commissioner Wu Shen looked down on his soldiers as weak and worked them harshly.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shen, observation commissioner of Fujian, looked down on his troops as weak and drove them with harsh labor.

sentences.zh: 軍士作亂，殺詵腹心十餘人，逼詵牒大將郝誡溢掌留務。

translations.literal: The soldiers mutinied, killed more than ten of Shen's close confidants, and forced Shen to issue an order putting senior general Hao Jie in acting charge of circuit affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers mutinied, killed more than ten of Shen's closest associates, and forced Shen to issue an order putting senior general Hao Jie in temporary command of the circuit.

sentences.zh: 誡溢上表請罪，上遣中使就赦以安之。

translations.literal: Jie submitted a memorial asking to be punished; the emperor sent a palace envoy to pardon and reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Jie submitted a memorial asking to be punished. The emperor sent a palace envoy to grant a pardon and restore order.

sentences.zh: 乙未，隴右節度使李元諒築良原故城而鎮之。

translations.literal: On the yimwei day, Longyou military commissioner Li Yuanliang built the old city of Liangyuan and garrisoned it.
translations.idiomatic: On the yimwei day, Li Yuanliang, military commissioner of Longyou, rebuilt the old city of Liangyuan and established his headquarters there.

sentences.zh: 雲南王異牟尋欲內附，未敢自遣使，先遣其東蠻鬼主驃旁、苴夢沖、苴烏星入見。

translations.literal: The King of Nanzhao, Yi Muxun, wished to submit to the interior but did not dare send his own envoy; he first sent his Eastern Man ghost-lords Piao Pang, Ju Mengchong, and Ju Wuxing to audience.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Muxun, king of Nanzhao, wished to submit to Tang rule but did not dare send his own envoy. He first sent three Eastern Man chieftains—Piao Pang, Ju Mengchong, and Ju Wuxing—to audience at court.

sentences.zh: 五月，乙卯，宴之於麟德殿，賜賚甚厚，封王給印而遣之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the yimao day, they were feasted in Linde Hall, richly rewarded, granted royal seals, and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the yimao day, the emperor feasted them in Linde Hall, gave them lavish gifts, conferred royal seals, and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 辛未，以太子賓客吳湊為福建觀察使，貶吳詵為涪州刺史。

translations.literal: On the xinwei day, crown prince guest Wu Cou was appointed Fujian observation commissioner, and Wu Shen was demoted to prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinwei day, Wu Cou, guest of the crown prince, was appointed observation commissioner of Fujian, and Wu Shen was demoted to prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃三萬餘騎寇涇、邠、寧、慶、鄜等州。

translations.literal: More than thirty thousand Tibetan horsemen raided the prefectures of Jing, Bin, Ning, Qing, and Fu.
translations.idiomatic: More than thirty thousand Tibetan cavalry raided the prefectures of Jing, Bin, Ning, Qing, and Fu.

sentences.zh: 先是，吐蕃常以秋冬入寇，及春多病疫退。

translations.literal: Previously the Tibetans had usually invaded in autumn and winter and withdrew in spring when plague was common.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the Tibetans had usually invaded in autumn and winter and withdrew in spring, when plague often broke out.

sentences.zh: 至是，得唐人，質其妻子，遣其將將之，盛夏入寇。

translations.literal: On this occasion they obtained Tang men, held their wives and children as hostages, and had their generals lead them in a midsummer invasion.
translations.idiomatic: This time they captured Tang subjects, held their families hostage, and used them to guide their generals in a midsummer invasion.

sentences.zh: 諸州皆城守，無敢與戰者，吐蕃俘掠人畜萬計而去。

translations.literal: All the prefectures held to their walls; none dared give battle, and the Tibetans carried off people and livestock by the tens of thousands before departing.
translations.idiomatic: Every prefecture held behind its walls; none dared give battle. The Tibetans seized people and livestock by the tens of thousands and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 夏縣人陽城以學行著聞，隱居柳谷之北，李泌薦之。

translations.literal: Yang Cheng of Xia County was renowned for learning and conduct and lived in seclusion north of Liugu Valley; Li Bi recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Cheng of Xia County was renowned for learning and integrity and lived in seclusion north of Liugu Valley. Li Bi recommended him.

sentences.zh: 六月徵拜諫議大夫。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he was summoned and appointed remonstrance and policy advisor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he was summoned to court and appointed remonstrance and policy advisor.

sentences.zh: 韓游瑰以吐蕃犯塞，自戍寧州。

translations.literal: Han Yougui, because the Tibetans violated the frontier, personally garrisoned Ning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Tibetans were raiding the frontier, Han Yougui personally garrisoned Ning Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 病，求代歸。

translations.literal: He fell ill and asked to be replaced and return.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill and asked to be relieved and allowed to return to court.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，庚戌，加渾瑊邠寧副元帥，以左金吾將軍張獻甫為邠寧節度使，陳許兵馬使韓全義為長武城行營節度使。

translations.literal: In autumn, in the seventh month, on the gengxu day, Hun Jian was promoted to deputy commander of Binning; Left Golden Guard general Zhang Xianfu was made Binning military commissioner, and Chenxu army commissioner Han Quanyi was made expeditionary military commissioner of Changwu Fort.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on the gengxu day, Hun Jian was promoted to deputy commander of Binning. Left Golden Guard general Zhang Xianfu was appointed military commissioner of Binning, and Han Quanyi, army commissioner of Chenxu, was appointed expeditionary military commissioner of Changwu Fort.

sentences.zh: 獻甫未至，壬子夜，游瑰不告於眾，輕騎歸朝。

translations.literal: Before Xianfu arrived, on the night of the renzi day, Yougui without informing the masses rode lightly back to court.
translations.idiomatic: Before Zhang Xianfu arrived, on the night of the renzi day, Yougui left without telling his troops and rode swiftly back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 戍卒裴滿等憚獻甫之嚴，乘無帥之際，癸丑，帥其徒作亂，曰：「張公不出本軍，我必拒之。

translations.literal: Garrison soldiers Pei Man and others feared Xianfu's severity; seizing the moment when there was no commander, on the guichou day they led their comrades in mutiny, saying, "If General Zhang does not come from this army, we will surely reject him.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison soldiers led by Pei Man feared Zhang Xianfu's strictness. Seizing the moment when the circuit had no commander, on the guichou day they mutinied and declared, "If General Zhang is not chosen from our own army, we will refuse him.

sentences.zh: 」因剽掠城市，圍監軍楊明義所居，使奏請范希朝為節度使。

translations.literal: They then plundered the city, surrounded the residence of army supervisor Yang Mingyi, and had him memorialize requesting Fan Xichao as military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: They then looted the city, surrounded army supervisor Yang Mingyi's residence, and forced him to memorialize requesting Fan Xichao as military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 都虞侯楊朝晟避亂出城，聞之，復入，曰：「所請甚契我心，我來賀也！

translations.literal: Chief adjutant Yang Zhaosheng fled the turmoil out of the city; hearing of it, he re-entered and said, "What you request accords very well with my heart—I have come to congratulate you!"
translations.idiomatic: Chief adjutant Yang Zhaosheng had fled the city during the chaos. When he heard what was happening, he went back in and said, "Your request matches my own wishes exactly—I have come to congratulate you!"

sentences.zh: 」亂卒稍安。

translations.literal: The mutinous soldiers gradually calmed.
translations.idiomatic: The mutineers gradually calmed down.

sentences.zh: 朝晟潛與諸將謀，晨勒兵，如亂卒謂曰：「所請不行，張公已至邠州，汝曹作亂當死，不可盡殺，宜自推列唱帥者。

translations.literal: Zhaosheng secretly plotted with the other generals; at dawn he marshaled troops, went to the mutineers and said, "Your request will not be granted; General Zhang has already reached Bin Prefecture. You who mutinied deserve death, but all cannot be killed—you should yourselves identify and list the ringleaders."
translations.idiomatic: Zhaosheng secretly plotted with the other generals. At dawn he assembled his troops, went to the mutineers, and said, "Your request has been denied. General Zhang has already reached Bin Prefecture. Mutiny is punishable by death, but we cannot kill you all—you should identify the ringleaders yourselves."

sentences.zh: 」遂斬二百餘人，帥眾迎獻甫。

translations.literal: He then beheaded more than two hundred men and led the masses to welcome Xianfu.
translations.idiomatic: He then executed more than two hundred men and led the troops out to welcome Zhang Xianfu.

sentences.zh: 上聞軍眾欲得范希朝，將授之。

translations.literal: The emperor heard that the army wanted Fan Xichao and was about to appoint him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard that the troops wanted Fan Xichao, he was about to appoint him.

sentences.zh: 希朝辭曰：「臣畏游瑰之禍而來，今往代之，非所以防窺覦，安反仄也。

translations.literal: Xichao declined, saying, "Your servant came here fearing Yougui's persecution; to go now and replace him is not the way to guard against covetous eyes and settle restless hearts."
translations.idiomatic: Xichao declined, saying, "I came to court because I feared Yougui's persecution. If I go now to replace him, that will not deter ambition or settle restless troops."

sentences.zh: 」上嘉之，擢為寧州刺史，以副獻甫。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him and promoted him to prefect of Ning Prefecture to assist Xianfu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him and promoted him to prefect of Ning Prefecture to serve under Zhang Xianfu.

sentences.zh: 游瑰至京師，除右龍武統軍。

translations.literal: Yougui reached the capital and was appointed commander of the Right Longwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Yougui reached the capital, he was appointed commander of the Right Longwu Army.

sentences.zh: 振武節度使唐朝臣不嚴斥候，己未，奚、室韋寇振武，執宣慰中使二人，大掠人畜而去。

translations.literal: Zhenwu military commissioner Tang Zhaochen did not strictly maintain scouts; on the jiwei day, the Xi and Shiwei raided Zhenwu, seized two palace envoys on a pacification mission, and carried off people and livestock in great numbers before departing.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Zhaochen, military commissioner of Zhenwu, failed to maintain proper scouting. On the jiwei day, the Xi and Shiwei raided Zhenwu, captured two palace envoys on a pacification mission, and carried off people and livestock in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 時回紇之眾逆公主者在振武，朝臣遣七百騎與回紇數百騎追之，回紇使者為奚、室韋所殺。

translations.literal: At the time Uyghur troops escorting the princess back were at Zhenwu; Zhaochen sent seven hundred horsemen with several hundred Uyghur horsemen in pursuit, and Uyghur envoys were killed by the Xi and Shiwei.
translations.idiomatic: Uyghur troops escorting the princess back were then stationed at Zhenwu. Zhaochen sent seven hundred horsemen together with several hundred Uyghur cavalry in pursuit, but Uyghur envoys were killed by the Xi and Shiwei.

sentences.zh: 九月，庚申，吐蕃尚志董星寇寧州，張獻甫擊卻之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the gengshen day, the Tibetan general Shangzhi Dongxing raided Ning Prefecture; Zhang Xianfu struck and repulsed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the gengshen day, the Tibetan general Shangzhi Dongxing raided Ning Prefecture. Zhang Xianfu attacked and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃轉掠鄜、坊而去。

translations.literal: The Tibetans turned to raid Fu and Fang before departing.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans then raided Fu and Fang prefectures before withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 元友直句檢諸道稅外物，悉輸戶部，遂為定制，歲於稅外輸百餘萬緡、斛，民不堪命。

translations.literal: Yuan Youzhi audited extra-tax goods from all circuits and had them all delivered to the Ministry of Revenue; this then became a fixed regulation, and each year more than a million strings and hu were delivered beyond regular taxes—the people could not bear the burden.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Youzhi audited extra-tax goods from all circuits and had them all remitted to the Ministry of Revenue. This became a permanent system, yielding more than a million strings of cash and hu of grain each year beyond regular taxes—a burden the people could not endure.

sentences.zh: 諸道多自訴於上，上意寤，詔：「今年已入在官者輸京師，未入者悉以與民；

translations.literal: The various circuits many on their own appealed to the emperor; the emperor's mind awakened, and he edicted: 'This year what has already entered and is in the officials — deliver to the capital; what has not entered — entirely give to the people;
translations.idiomatic: Officials from many circuits petitioned the emperor on their own account. When he grasped the situation, he issued an edict: whatever extra-tax goods had already been entered into government stores this year were to be sent to the capital; whatever had not yet been entered was to be returned entirely to the people.

sentences.zh: 明年以後，悉免之。

translations.literal: From next year onward, entirely exempt them.
translations.idiomatic: From the following year onward, the levy would be abolished altogether.

sentences.zh: 」於是東南之民復安其業。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon the people of the southeast again settled their occupations in peace.
translations.idiomatic: With that, the people of the southeast were able to resume their livelihoods in peace.

sentences.zh: 回紇合骨咄祿可汗得唐許婚，甚喜，遣其妹骨咄祿毘伽公主及大臣妻並國相、趺跌都督以下千餘人來迎可敦，辭禮甚恭，曰：「昔為兄弟，今為子婿，半子也。

translations.literal: The Uyghur khagan Qapaghan, having obtained Tang permission for marriage, was greatly pleased; he sent his younger sister Princess Qutluq Bilge and the ministers' wives together with the kingdom's chancellor, the Diexie governors, and more than a thousand persons below them to welcome the imperial consort. Their words and rites were very deferential, saying: 'Formerly we were brothers; now we are son-in-law and father-in-law — half a son.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghur khagan Qapaghan, delighted that Tang had granted the marriage alliance, sent his younger sister Princess Qutluq Bilge, the wives of his ministers, the kingdom's chancellor, the Diexie governors, and more than a thousand persons of rank to welcome the imperial bride. Their language and ceremony were most respectful: 'Once we stood as brothers; now we are son-in-law and father-in-law — in effect, half a son.

sentences.zh: 若吐蕃為患，子當為父除之！

translations.literal: If Tibet becomes a calamity, the son ought to eliminate it for the father!
translations.idiomatic: If the Tibetans bring trouble, the son shall remove the threat for his father-in-law!

sentences.zh: 」因詈辱吐蕃使者以絕之。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon they reviled and humiliated the Tibetan envoys to break with them.
translations.idiomatic: They then reviled and humiliated the Tibetan envoys, severing relations with Tibet.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，戊子，回紇至長安，可汗仍表請改回紇為回鶻，許之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day wuzi, the Uyghurs reached Chang'an; the khagan again memorialized requesting that Huihe be changed to Huihu, and permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on the day wuzi, the Uyghurs arrived at Chang'an. The khagan again petitioned to change the name from Huihe to Huihu, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃發兵十萬將寇西川，亦發雲南兵。

translations.literal: Tibet raised troops numbering one hundred thousand and was about to raid western Sichuan; it also mobilized Yunnan troops.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet mobilized a hundred thousand men for a planned invasion of western Sichuan and also called up Yunnan forces.

sentences.zh: 雲南內雖附唐，外未敢叛吐蕃，亦發兵數萬屯於瀘北。

translations.literal: Though Yunnan inwardly had submitted to Tang, outwardly it did not dare rebel against Tibet; it too raised several tens of thousands of troops and encamped north of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan was inwardly aligned with Tang but still dared not openly break with Tibet; it likewise raised tens of thousands of troops and encamped north of the Lu River.

sentences.zh: 韋皋知雲南計方猶豫，乃為書遺雲南王，敘其叛吐蕃歸化之誠，貯以銀函，使東蠻轉致吐蕃。

translations.literal: Wei Gao knew that Yunnan's plans were still wavering; he therefore wrote a letter to the king of Yunnan describing the sincerity of turning from Tibet and submitting to Tang, stored it in a silver casket, and had the Eastern Barbarians relay it to Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that Yunnan was still hesitating, Wei Gao wrote to its king affirming his sincerity in abandoning Tibet and returning to Tang, sealed the letter in a silver box, and had the Eastern Barbarians deliver it to the Tibetans.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃始疑雲南，遣兵二萬屯會川，以塞雲南趣蜀之路。

translations.literal: Tibet then began to suspect Yunnan; it sent twenty thousand troops to encamp at Huichuan to block Yunnan's route toward Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet now grew suspicious of Yunnan and sent twenty thousand men to garrison Huichuan, blocking the road by which Yunnan could advance toward Shu.

sentences.zh: 雲南怒，引兵歸國。

translations.literal: Yunnan, enraged, led its troops back to its own country.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Yunnan withdrew its army and returned home.

sentences.zh: 由是雲南與吐蕃相猜阻，歸唐之志益堅。

translations.literal: From this Yunnan and Tibet mutually suspected and obstructed each other; the resolve to return to Tang grew firmer.
translations.idiomatic: Mutual suspicion and obstruction now arose between Yunnan and Tibet, and Yunnan's determination to rejoin Tang only hardened.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃失雲南之助，兵勢始弱矣。

translations.literal: Tibet lost Yunnan's aid, and its military strength began to weaken.
translations.idiomatic: Deprived of Yunnan's support, Tibet's military position began to weaken.

sentences.zh: 然吐蕃業已入寇，遂分兵四萬攻兩林驃旁，三萬攻東蠻，七千寇清溪關，五千寇銅山。

translations.literal: Yet Tibet had already entered in raid; it then divided its forces — forty thousand to attack the Lianglin and Piao tribes, thirty thousand to attack the Eastern Barbarians, seven thousand to raid Qingxi Pass, five thousand to raid Tongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet had already launched its invasion, however, and now split its army: forty thousand to strike the Lianglin and Piao peoples, thirty thousand against the Eastern Barbarians, seven thousand against Qingxi Pass, and five thousand against Tongshan.

sentences.zh: 皋遣黎州刺史韋晉等與東蠻連兵御之，破吐蕃於清溪關外。

translations.literal: Gao sent Li Prefecture governor Wei Jin and others to join forces with the Eastern Barbarians in defense and defeated Tibet outside Qingxi Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gao sent Li Prefecture governor Wei Jin and others to combine with the Eastern Barbarians in defense and routed the Tibetans outside Qingxi Pass.

sentences.zh: 庚子，冊命咸安公主，加回鶻可汗號長壽天親可汗。

translations.literal: On the day gengzi, Princess Xian'an was invested by edict, and the Uyghur khagan was given the title Longevity and Heavenly Kin Khagan.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengzi, Princess Xian'an received her investiture, and the Uyghur khagan was granted the title Longevity and Heavenly Kin Khagan.

sentences.zh: 十一月，以刑部尚書關播為送咸安公主兼冊回鶻可汗使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Guan Bo, Minister of Justice, was appointed envoy to escort Princess Xian'an and concurrently invest the Uyghur khagan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Guan Bo, Minister of Justice, was appointed envoy to escort Princess Xian'an and invest the Uyghur khagan.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃恥前日之敗，復以眾二萬寇清溪關，一萬攻東蠻。

translations.literal: Ashamed of its defeat the previous day, Tibet again sent twenty thousand to raid Qingxi Pass and ten thousand to attack the Eastern Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Stung by its recent defeat, Tibet again sent twenty thousand men against Qingxi Pass and ten thousand against the Eastern Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 韋皋命韋晉鎮要沖城，督諸軍以御之。

translations.literal: Wei Gao ordered Wei Jin to garrison Yaichong Fort and direct all armies in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gao ordered Wei Jin to hold Yaichong Fort and supervise the various armies in repelling the attack.

sentences.zh: 巂州經略使劉朝彩等出關連戰，自乙卯至癸亥，大破之。

translations.literal: Xi's circuit defense commissioner Liu Chaocai and others sallied from the pass and fought in succession from the day yimao to the day guihai, inflicting a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's defense commissioner Liu Chaocai and others marched out of the pass and fought continuously from the day yimao through the day guihai, winning a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 李泌言於上曰：「江、淮漕運，自淮入汴，以甬橋為咽喉，地屬徐州，鄰於李納，刺史高明應年少不習事，若李納一旦復有異圖，竊據徐州，是失江、淮也，國用何從而致！

translations.literal: Li Mi said to the emperor: 'The Jiang and Huai grain transport, from the Huai entering the Bian Canal, takes Yongqiao as its throat; the territory belongs to Xuzhou and borders Li Na. The prefect Gao Mingying is young and unskilled in affairs. If Li Na should one day again harbor a different design and seize Xuzhou by stealth, that would mean losing the Jiang and Huai — whence would state revenue come!
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi said to the emperor: 'Grain transport on the Jiang and Huai routes enters the Bian Canal from the Huai; Yongqiao is the vital choke point. That ground belongs to Xuzhou and lies next to Li Na's territory. Prefect Gao Mingying is young and inexperienced. If Li Na should ever again turn disloyal and seize Xuzhou, we would lose the Jiang and Huai — and with them the state's revenue.

sentences.zh: 請徙壽、廬、濠都團練使張建封鎮徐州，割濠、泗以隸之。

translations.literal: I request that Zhang Jianfeng, regimental training commissioner of Shou, Lu, and Hao, be transferred to garrison Xuzhou, and that Hao and Si be severed to fall under his command.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Zhang Jianfeng, regimental training commissioner of Shou, Lu, and Hao, be posted to Xuzhou, with Hao and Si detached and placed under his authority.

sentences.zh: 復以廬、壽歸淮南，則淄青惕息而運路常通，江、淮安矣。

translations.literal: If Lu and Shou are restored to Huainan, then Ziqing will be restrained and the transport routes kept constantly open — the Jiang and Huai will be secure.
translations.idiomatic: Restore Lu and Shou to Huainan, and Ziqing will be kept in check while the transport lines stay open — the Jiang and Huai will be secure.

sentences.zh: 及今明應幼騃可代，宜徵為金吾將軍。

translations.literal: While Gao Mingying is still young and callow and can be replaced, he should be summoned and made a general of the Jinwu Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Mingying is still young and untested and can be replaced now; summon him and appoint him a general of the Jinwu Guard.

sentences.zh: 萬一使它人得之，則不可復製矣。

translations.literal: If by any chance another person obtained it, it could never be recovered.
translations.idiomatic: If someone else were to seize it, recovery would be impossible.

sentences.zh: 」上從之。

translations.literal: ' The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted the proposal.

sentences.zh: 以建封為徐、泗、濠節度使。

translations.literal: Zhang Jianfeng was made military governor of Xu, Si, and Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jianfeng was appointed military governor of Xu, Si, and Hao.

sentences.zh: 建封為政寬厚而有綱紀，不貸人以法，故其下無不畏而悅之。

translations.literal: Jianfeng's governance was generous and yet had discipline; he did not excuse anyone from the law. Therefore his subordinates all both feared and were pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng governed with generosity and firm discipline alike; he showed no favoritism before the law. His men feared him and yet admired him.

sentences.zh: 橫海節度使程日華薨，子懷直自知留後。

translations.literal: Cheng Rihua, military governor of Henghai, died; his son Huai zhi declared himself acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Rihua, military governor of Henghai, died; his son Huai zhi installed himself as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃屢遣人誘脅雲南。

translations.literal: Tibet repeatedly sent men to entice and coerce Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet repeatedly sent agents to entice and intimidate Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 德宗神武聖文皇帝八貞元五年（

translations.literal: The eighth year of Emperor Dezong's Zhenyuan reign (
translations.idiomatic: The eighth year of Emperor Dezong's Zhenyuan reign (

sentences.zh: 己巳，公元七八九年）

translations.literal: jisi, 789 CE)
translations.idiomatic: jisi, 789 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，二月，丁亥，韋皋遺異牟尋書，稱：「回鶻屢請佐天子共滅吐蕃，王不早定計，一旦為回鶻所先，則王累代功名虛棄矣。

translations.literal: In spring, the second month, on the day dinghai, Wei Gao sent a letter to Nanzhao's Yi Muxun, stating: 'The Uyghurs have repeatedly asked to assist the Son of Heaven in destroying Tibet together. If Your Majesty does not decide soon and the Uyghurs act first, then Your Majesty's achievements through successive generations will be wasted in vain.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the second month, on the day dinghai, Wei Gao wrote to Nanzhao's Yi Muxun: 'The Uyghurs have repeatedly offered to join the Son of Heaven in destroying Tibet. If you do not decide quickly and the Uyghurs move first, the glory your house has won through generations will come to nothing.

sentences.zh: 且雲南久為吐蕃屈辱，今不乘此時依大國之勢以復怨雪恥，後悔無及矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, Yunnan has long suffered humiliation at Tibet's hands; if you do not now seize this moment and rely on the great state's power to repay grievances and wash away shame, later regret will be too late.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan has endured Tibet's humiliations for years. Fail to use the great power of the empire now to settle old scores and restore your honor, and you will regret it when it is too late.

sentences.zh: 」戊戌，以橫海留後程懷直為滄州觀察使。

translations.literal: ' On the day wuxu, Cheng Huai zhi, acting governor of Henghai, was made observation commissioner of Cang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuxu, Cheng Huai zhi, acting governor of Henghai, was appointed observation commissioner of Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 懷直請分景城、弓高為景州，仍請朝廷除刺史。

translations.literal: Huai zhi requested that Jingcheng and Gonggao be separated out as Jing Prefecture and further asked the court to appoint a prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Huai zhi asked that Jingcheng and Gonggao be carved out as Jing Prefecture and requested that the court appoint a prefect.

sentences.zh: 上喜曰：「三十年無此事矣！

translations.literal: The emperor said with pleasure: 'For thirty years there has been nothing like this!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said delightedly: 'Nothing like this has happened in thirty years!

sentences.zh: 」乃以員外郎徐伸為景州刺史。

translations.literal: ' He then appointed Xu Shen, an outer-office official, prefect of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He then appointed outer-office official Xu Shen prefect of Jing.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎、同平章事李泌屢乞更命相。

translations.literal: Li Mi, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor, repeatedly begged to be replaced as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor, repeatedly asked to be relieved of his post as chief minister.

sentences.zh: 上欲用戶部侍郎班宏，泌言宏雖清強而性多凝滯，乃薦竇參通敏，可兼度支鹽鐵；

translations.literal: The emperor wished to use Ban Hong, Vice Minister of Revenue; Mi said that although Hong was upright and forceful, his nature was much given to hesitation and obstruction, and therefore recommended Dou Can as quick and perceptive, fit to hold concurrently the posts of fiscal transport and salt and iron;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to appoint Ban Hong, Vice Minister of Revenue. Mi said that while Hong was upright and capable, he was overly cautious and slow; he therefore recommended Dou Can as quick-witted and fit to oversee fiscal transport and the salt and iron monopolies concurrently.

sentences.zh: 董晉方正，可處門下。

translations.literal: Dong Jin was upright and could serve in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Jin was upright and suited to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 上皆以為不可。

translations.literal: The emperor considered both unsuitable.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejected both recommendations.

sentences.zh: 參，誕之玄孫也，時為御史中丞兼戶部侍郎；

translations.literal: Can was the great-grandson of Dou Yan and at the time was Censor-in-Chief and concurrent Vice Minister of Revenue;
translations.idiomatic: Can was the great-grandson of Dou Yan and then served as Censor-in-Chief and concurrent Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 晉為太常卿。

translations.literal: Jin was Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 至是泌疾甚，復薦二人。

translations.literal: By this time Mi's illness was severe, and he again recommended the two men.
translations.idiomatic: By then Mi was gravely ill and once more recommended the two men.

sentences.zh: 庚子，以董晉為門下侍郎，竇參為中書侍郎兼度支轉運使，並同平章事。

translations.literal: On the day gengzi, Dong Jin was made Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Dou Can was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and concurrent Commissioner of Fiscal Transport; both became Grand Councilors.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengzi, Dong Jin was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Dou Can Vice Director of the Secretariat and Commissioner of Fiscal Transport; both were made Grand Councilors.

sentences.zh: 以班宏為尚書，依前度支轉運副使。

translations.literal: Ban Hong was made a Minister and continued as Deputy Commissioner of Fiscal Transport as before.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Hong was promoted to Minister and retained his post as Deputy Commissioner of Fiscal Transport.

sentences.zh: 參為人剛果峭刻，無學術，多權數，每奏事，諸相出，參獨居後，以奏度支事為辭，實專大政，多引親黨置要地，使為耳目。

translations.literal: Can was by nature resolute, sharp, and harsh; he had no learning and relied much on stratagems. Whenever he reported on affairs, after the other councilors left, Can alone remained behind, using fiscal business as his pretext; in fact he monopolized major policy, placing many kinsmen and partisans in key posts to serve as his eyes and ears.
translations.idiomatic: Can was hard, decisive, and cutting; he lacked scholarly training and trafficked in schemes. After each audience, when the other councilors withdrew, Can alone lingered behind on the pretext of fiscal business and in practice seized control of major policy. He placed relatives and allies in key posts to serve as his eyes and ears.

sentences.zh: 董晉充位而已。

translations.literal: Dong Jin merely filled the seat.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Jin held the title and nothing more.

sentences.zh: 然晉為人重慎，所言於上前者未嘗洩於人，子弟或問之，晉曰：「欲知宰相能否，視天下安危。

translations.literal: Yet Jin was by nature grave and cautious; what he said before the emperor he never leaked to others. When his sons and younger brothers asked him, Jin said: 'To know whether a chief minister is capable, look at the safety or peril of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Jin, however, was grave and cautious by nature and never disclosed to others what he had said before the throne. When his sons and brothers asked him, he replied: 'Judge a chief minister by whether the realm is safe or in peril.

sentences.zh: 所謀議於上前者，不足道也。

translations.literal: What is deliberated before the emperor is not worth discussing.
translations.idiomatic: The words exchanged before the emperor are not the measure of the man.

sentences.zh: 」三月，甲辰，李泌薨。

translations.literal: ' In the third month, on the day jiachen, Li Mi died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the day jiachen, Li Mi died.

sentences.zh: 泌有謀略而好談神仙詭誕，故為世所輕。

translations.literal: Mi had stratagem and yet loved to speak of immortals and the bizarre; therefore the age held him lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Mi was a man of strategy, yet he loved to talk of immortals and marvels, and for that the world undervalued him.

sentences.zh: 初，上思李懷光之功，欲宥其一子，而子孫皆已伏誅。

translations.literal: Earlier, the emperor recalled Li Huaiguang's service and wished to spare one of his sons, but his sons and grandsons had all already been executed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor, mindful of Li Huaiguang's past service, had wished to spare one of his sons, but all his sons and grandsons had already been put to death.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，詔以懷光外孫燕八八為懷光後，賜姓名李承緒，除左衛率冑曹參軍，賜錢千緡，使養懷光妻王氏及守其基祀。

translations.literal: On the day wuchen, an edict made Huaiguang's grandson by his daughter, Yan Baba, Huaiguang's heir, granted him the name Li Chengxu, appointed him Army Adjutant of the Left Guard, gave him a thousand strings of cash, and charged him to support Huaiguang's wife Lady Wang and maintain his ancestral rites.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuchen, an edict adopted Huaiguang's daughter's son Yan Baba as his heir, bestowed on him the name Li Chengxu, appointed him Army Adjutant of the Left Guard, granted a thousand strings of cash, and charged him with supporting Huaiguang's widow Lady Wang and maintaining the family sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，韋皋遣其將王有道將兵與東蠻、兩林蠻及吐蕃青海、臘城二節度戰於巂州台登谷，大破之，斬首二千級，投崖及溺死者不可勝數，殺其大兵馬使乞藏遮遮。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Wei Gao sent his general Wang Youdao with troops to join the Eastern Barbarians, the Lianglin tribes, and Tibet's Qinghai and Lacheng circuit armies in battle at Taideng Valley in Xi Prefecture, inflicting a great defeat: two thousand heads cut off, incalculable numbers cast from cliffs or drowned, and the great cavalry commander Qizang Zhezhe killed.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Wei Gao sent his general Wang Youdao with troops to fight at Taideng Valley in Xi Prefecture alongside the Eastern Barbarians, the Lianglin tribes, and the Tibetan Qinghai and Lacheng circuit forces. He won a great victory, taking two thousand heads; countless men were hurled from cliffs or drowned; and the enemy's great cavalry commander Qizang Zhezhe was killed.

sentences.zh: 乞藏遮遮，虜之驍將也，既死，皋所攻城柵無不下。

translations.literal: Qizang Zhezhe was a fierce general of the barbarians; once he was dead, none of the fortresses and stockades Gao besieged failed to fall.
translations.idiomatic: Qizang Zhezhe had been the enemy's boldest commander; after his death, every fortress and stockade Wei Gao attacked fell.

sentences.zh: 數年，盡復巂州之境。

translations.literal: Within several years, he fully recovered the territory of Xi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years he had fully recovered the territory of Xi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 易定節度使張孝忠興兵襲蔚州，驅掠人畜。

translations.literal: Zhang Xiaozhong, military governor of Yiding, raised troops and raided Yu Prefecture, driving off and plundering people and livestock.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiaozhong, military governor of Yiding, mobilized troops, raided Yu Prefecture, and drove off people and livestock.

sentences.zh: 詔書責之，逾旬還鎮。

translations.literal: An imperial letter rebuked him; after more than ten days he returned to his command.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial rebuke was sent; after ten days he returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 瓊州自乾封中為山賊所陷，至是，嶺南節度使李復遣判官姜孟京與崖州刺史張少遷攻拔之。

translations.literal: Qiong Prefecture had been lost to mountain bandits since the Qianfeng era; by this time Lingnan military governor Li Fu sent judge Jiang Mengjing and Ya Prefecture governor Zhang Shaoqian to attack and recover it.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong Prefecture had fallen to mountain bandits since the Qianfeng period; now Lingnan military governor Li Fu sent judge Jiang Mengjing and Ya Prefecture governor Zhang Shaoqian to attack and retake it.

sentences.zh: 十二月，庚午，聞回鶻天親可汗薨，戊寅，遣鴻臚卿郭鋒冊命其子為登裡羅沒密施俱祿忠貞毘伽可汗。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day gengwu, word came that the Uyghur Longevity and Heavenly Kin Khagan had died; on the day wuyin, Guo Feng, Minister of Hospitality, was sent to invest his son as Dengli Luomei Mishijulu Zhongzhen Bilge Khagan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day gengwu, news arrived that the Uyghur Longevity and Heavenly Kin Khagan had died. On the day wuyin, Guo Feng, Minister of Hospitality, was dispatched to invest the son as Dengli Luomei Mishijulu Zhongzhen Bilge Khagan.

sentences.zh: 先是，安西、北庭皆假道於回鶻以奏事，故與之連和。

translations.literal: Earlier, Anxi and Beiting had both relied on passage through the Uyghurs to report affairs to the court, and therefore maintained alliance with them.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, both Anxi and Beiting had depended on the Uyghurs for passage when reporting to court, and so remained allied with them.

sentences.zh: 北庭去回鶻猶近，回鶻誅求無厭，又有沙陀六千餘帳與北庭相依。

translations.literal: Beiting was still close to the Uyghurs; the Uyghurs' exactions were insatiable, and moreover more than six thousand Shatuo households were linked with Beiting.
translations.idiomatic: Beiting lay close to Uyghur territory; the Uyghurs' demands were never-ending, and more than six thousand Shatuo households were bound to Beiting.

sentences.zh: 及三葛祿、白服突厥皆附於回鶻，回鶻數侵掠之。

translations.literal: When the Three Karluk tribes and the White-clad Turks all attached themselves to the Uyghurs, the Uyghurs repeatedly raided them.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Three Karluk tribes and the White-clad Turks had submitted to the Uyghurs, the Uyghurs repeatedly preyed on them.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃因葛祿、白服之眾以攻北庭，回鶻大相頡干迦斯將兵救之。

translations.literal: Tibet used the Karluk and White-clad forces to attack Beiting; the Uyghur great chancellor Bogu Qarakhuz led troops to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet drew on the Karluk and White-clad peoples to attack Beiting, and the Uyghur great chancellor Bogu Qarakhuz marched to its relief.

sentences.zh: 雲南雖貳於吐蕃，亦未敢顯與之絕。

translations.literal: Though Yunnan had turned disloyal toward Tibet, it still did not dare openly break with it.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan had already wavered in its loyalty to Tibet, yet still dared not break openly with it.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，韋皋復以書招諭之。

translations.literal: On the day renchen, Wei Gao again wrote to summon and instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renchen, Wei Gao again wrote to summon and persuade them.

sentences.zh: 德宗神武聖文皇帝八貞元六年（

translations.literal: The ninth year of Emperor Dezong's Zhenyuan reign (
translations.idiomatic: The ninth year of Emperor Dezong's Zhenyuan reign (

sentences.zh: 庚午，公元七九零年）

translations.literal: gengwu, 790 CE)
translations.idiomatic: gengwu, 790 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，詔出岐山無憂王寺佛指骨迎置禁中，又送諸寺以示眾，傾都瞻禮，施財巨萬；

translations.literal: In spring, an edict ordered the Buddha's finger bone brought out from Wuyouwang Temple on Mount Qi, received into the palace, and then sent to various temples to be shown to the people; the whole capital turned out to pay homage, and donations ran to vast sums;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, an edict brought the Buddha's finger bone out from Wuyouwang Temple on Mount Qi into the palace, then sent it to temples throughout the capital for public veneration. The city poured forth to worship, and offerings amounted to vast sums.

sentences.zh: 二月，乙亥，遣中使復葬故處。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day yihai, palace envoys were sent to reinter it in its former place.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day yihai, palace envoys were sent to return the relic to its original resting place.

sentences.zh: 初，朱滔敗於貝州，其棣州刺史趙鎬以州降於王武俊，既而得罪於武俊，召之不至。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhu Tao was defeated at Bei Prefecture, his Di Prefecture governor Zhao Gao had surrendered the prefecture to Wang Wujun; afterward he gave offense to Wujun, and when summoned he did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Zhu Tao's defeat at Bei Prefecture, his Di Prefecture governor Zhao Gao had surrendered the prefecture to Wang Wujun; later he fell out with Wujun, and when summoned he refused to come.

sentences.zh: 田緒殘忍，其兄朝，仕李納為齊州刺史。

translations.literal: Tian Xu was cruel; his elder brother Chao served Li Na as prefect of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Xu was ruthless; his elder brother Chao served Li Na as prefect of Qi.

sentences.zh: 或言納欲納朝於魏，緒懼；

translations.literal: Some said Na wished to bring Chao into Wei; Xu was afraid;
translations.idiomatic: Word spread that Li Na meant to bring Chao into Wei; Xu grew alarmed.

sentences.zh: 判官孫光佐等為緒謀，厚賂納，且說納招趙鎬取棣州以悅之，因請送朝於京師。

translations.literal: Judge Sun Guangzuo and others plotted for Xu, bribing Na heavily and moreover urging Na to win over Zhao Gao and take Di Prefecture to please him, while also asking that Chao be sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Judge Sun Guangzuo and others devised a plan for Xu: they lavished bribes on Li Na and urged him to win Zhao Gao over and seize Di Prefecture as a gift, while also requesting that Chao be sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 納從之。

translations.literal: Na followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Li Na agreed.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，鎬以棣州降於納。

translations.literal: On the day dingyou, Gao surrendered Di Prefecture to Na.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingyou, Zhao Gao surrendered Di Prefecture to Li Na.

sentences.zh: 三月，武俊使其子士真擊之，不克。

translations.literal: In the third month, Wujun sent his son Shizhen to attack him but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Wang Wujun sent his son Shizhen to attack but failed to retake the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 回鶻忠貞可汗之弟弒忠貞而自立，其大相頡干迦斯西擊吐蕃未還，夏，四月，次相帥國人殺篡者而立忠貞之子阿啜為可汗，年十五。

translations.literal: The younger brother of the Uyghur Loyal and Chaste Khagan assassinated the Loyal and Chaste Khagan and installed himself. The great chancellor Bogu Qarakhuz had gone west to strike Tibet and had not yet returned. In summer, the fourth month, the secondary chancellor led the people to kill the usurper and install the Loyal and Chaste Khagan's son Achuo as khagan; he was fifteen years old.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghur Loyal and Chaste Khagan's younger brother murdered him and seized the throne. The great chancellor Bogu Qarakhuz was campaigning against Tibet in the west and had not returned. In summer, the fourth month, the secondary chancellor led the nation to kill the usurper and set the Loyal and Chaste Khagan's son Achuo on the throne; he was fifteen.

sentences.zh: 五月，王武俊屯冀州，將擊趙鎬，鎬帥其屬奔鄆州。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Wang Wujun encamped at Ji Prefecture and was about to attack Zhao Gao; Gao led his followers and fled to Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Wang Wujun encamped at Ji Prefecture intending to strike Zhao Gao; Gao fled with his followers to Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 李納分兵據之。

translations.literal: Li Na divided troops and occupied it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Na sent troops to occupy it.

sentences.zh: 田緒使孫光佐如鄆州，矯詔以棣州隸納。

translations.literal: Tian Xu sent Sun Guangzuo to Yan Prefecture and forged an edict placing Di Prefecture under Na's authority.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Xu sent Sun Guangzuo to Yan Prefecture with a forged edict placing Di Prefecture under Li Na.

sentences.zh: 武俊怒，遣其子士清伐貝州，取經城等四縣。

translations.literal: Wujun, enraged, sent his son Shiqing to attack Bei Prefecture and took Jingcheng and three other counties.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Wang Wujun sent his son Shiqing against Bei Prefecture and seized Jingcheng and three other counties.

sentences.zh: 回鶻頡干迦斯與吐蕃戰不利，吐蕃急攻北庭。

translations.literal: The Uyghur Bogu Qarakhuz fought Tibet with ill fortune; Tibet pressed the attack on Beiting.
translations.idiomatic: Bogu Qarakhuz's battle with Tibet went badly, and Tibet pressed hard against Beiting.

sentences.zh: 北庭人苦於回鶻誅求，與沙陀酋長朱邪盡忠皆降於吐蕃。

translations.literal: The people of Beiting, worn down by Uyghur exactions, together with the Shatuo chieftain Zhuye Jinzhong all surrendered to Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Beiting's people, exhausted by Uyghur exactions, joined Shatuo chieftain Zhuye Jinzhong in surrendering to Tibet.

sentences.zh: 節度使楊襲古帥麾下二千人奔西州。

translations.literal: Military governor Yang Xigu led two thousand men under his command and fled to Xi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Military governor Yang Xigu fled to Xi Prefecture with two thousand men.

sentences.zh: 六月，頡干迦斯引兵還國，次相恐其有廢立，與可汗皆出郊迎，俯伏自陳擅立之狀，曰：「今日惟大相死生之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Bogu Qarakhuz led his troops back to the realm. The secondary chancellor, fearing he might depose and install a ruler, together with the khagan went out to the suburbs to welcome him, prostrated themselves, and confessed their unauthorized enthronement, saying: 'Today we leave life and death entirely to the great chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Bogu Qarakhuz returned home with his army. Fearing he might overturn the succession, the secondary chancellor and the khagan went out to meet him in the suburbs, prostrated themselves, and confessed that they had enthroned the boy without authority: 'Today our lives are entirely in the great chancellor's hands.

sentences.zh: 」盛陳郭鋒所□國信，悉以遺之。

translations.literal: ' They lavishly displayed the imperial credentials [sent] by Guo Feng and gave them all to him.
translations.idiomatic: They then displayed in full the imperial credentials and gifts Guo Feng had brought and presented them all to him.

sentences.zh: 可汗拜且泣曰：「兒愚幼，若幸而得立，惟仰食於阿多，國政不敢豫也。

translations.literal: The khagan bowed and wept, saying: 'I am foolish and young; if by good fortune I am established, I shall rely on Father Aduo for my sustenance and dare not interfere in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The khagan bowed and wept: 'I am young and foolish; if I am fortunate enough to reign, I shall depend on Father Aduo for my very livelihood and will not presume to meddle in affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 」虜謂父為阿多，頡干迦斯感其卑屈，持之而哭，遂執臣禮，悉以所遺頒從行者，己無所受。

translations.literal: ' The barbarians call a father aduo. Bogu Qarakhuz was moved by this humility; he embraced him and wept, then performed the rites of a subject, distributing everything that had been presented among those who had accompanied him and accepting nothing himself.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Uyghurs, 'aduo' means father. Moved by such abasement, Bogu Qarakhuz held him and wept, then took the posture of a subject; he distributed all the gifts among his followers and kept nothing for himself.

sentences.zh: 國中由是稍安。

translations.literal: From this the realm gradually settled.
translations.idiomatic: The realm gradually regained its calm.

sentences.zh: 秋，頡干迦斯悉舉國兵數萬，召楊襲古，將復北庭，又為吐蕃所敗，死者大半。

translations.literal: In autumn, Bogu Qarakhuz mustered the entire nation's army, numbering tens of thousands, summoned Yang Xigu, and intended to recover Beiting; he was again defeated by Tibet, and more than half his men died.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Bogu Qarakhuz raised the whole nation's army, tens of thousands strong, called on Yang Xigu, and marched to retake Beiting; Tibet defeated him again, and more than half his force perished.

sentences.zh: 襲古收餘眾數百，將還西州，頡干迦斯紿之曰：「且與我同至牙帳，當送君還朝。

translations.literal: Xigu gathered the several hundred survivors and was about to return to Xi Prefecture; Bogu Qarakhuz deceived him, saying: 'For now come with me to the royal camp; I shall send you back to court.
translations.idiomatic: Xigu gathered the few hundred survivors and prepared to return to Xi Prefecture. Bogu Qarakhuz deceived him: 'Come first to my camp; I will then send you back to court.

sentences.zh: 」既而留不遣，竟殺之。

translations.literal: ' Afterward he detained him and would not release him, and in the end killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Once there, he held him and refused to let him go; in the end he had him killed.

sentences.zh: 安西由是遂絕，莫知存亡，而西州猶為唐固守。

translations.literal: Anxi was thereby cut off, and none knew whether it still survived; yet Xi Prefecture was still firmly held for Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Anxi was thus severed from the empire, and no one knew whether it still stood; Xi Prefecture alone remained loyally held for Tang.

sentences.zh: 葛祿乘勝取回鶻之浮圖川，回鶻震恐，悉遷西北部落於牙帳之南以避之。

translations.literal: The Karluks, following up their victory, took the Uyghurs' Futuchuan; the Uyghurs were shaken with fear and moved all their northwestern tribes south of the royal camp to avoid them.
translations.idiomatic: The Karluks, pressing their advantage, seized the Uyghurs' Futuchuan. Terrified, the Uyghurs shifted all their northwestern tribes south of the royal camp to escape them.

sentences.zh: 遣達北特勒梅錄隨郭鋒偕來，告忠貞可汗之喪，且求冊命。

translations.literal: They sent Tabo Tegin Meilu to come together with Guo Feng, announcing the Loyal and Chaste Khagan's death and also requesting investiture.
translations.idiomatic: They dispatched Tabo Tegin Meilu to accompany Guo Feng, announcing the Loyal and Chaste Khagan's death and seeking a new investiture from Tang.

sentences.zh: 先是，回鶻使者入中國，禮容驕慢，刺史皆與之鈞禮。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Uyghur envoys entered China, their bearing was arrogant and insolent, and prefects all exchanged equal courtesies with them.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, when Uyghur envoys arrived in China, they carried themselves with arrogant insolence, and prefects treated them as equals in ceremony.

sentences.zh: 梅錄至豐州，刺史李景略欲以氣加之，謂梅錄曰：「聞可汗新沒，欲申吊禮。

translations.literal: Meilu arrived at Feng Prefecture; Prefect Li Jinglve wished to overawe him with stern bearing and said to Meilu: 'I hear the khagan has newly died; I wish to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: When Meilu reached Feng Prefecture, Prefect Li Jinglve resolved to break his arrogance with sheer force of bearing. He told Meilu, 'I hear your khagan has just died; I wish to offer my condolences.

sentences.zh: 」景略先據高壟而坐，梅錄俯僂前哭。

translations.literal: ' Jinglve first took a raised mound and sat upon it; Meilu bowed low and came forward weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Jinglve seated himself first on a raised platform. Meilu bowed low and stepped forward to weep.

sentences.zh: 景略撫之曰：「可汗棄代，助爾哀慕。

translations.literal: Jinglve comforted him, saying: 'The khagan has left this world; let me share in your grief.
translations.idiomatic: Jinglve patted him and said, 'Your khagan has departed this life; let me mourn with you.

sentences.zh: 」梅錄驕容猛氣索然俱盡。

translations.literal: ' Meilu's arrogant mien and fierce spirit altogether vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Meilu's haughty bearing and fierce temper drained away entirely.

sentences.zh: 自是回鶻使至，皆拜景略於庭，威名聞塞外。

translations.literal: From this onward, whenever Uyghur envoys arrived, they all bowed to Jinglve in the courtyard; his reputation for stern authority spread beyond the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: After that, every Uyghur envoy who arrived bowed to Jinglve in the courtyard. His name for stern authority spread far beyond the passes.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，辛亥，郭鋒始自回鶻還。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, on the day xinhai, Guo Feng at last returned from the Uyghurs.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on the day xinhai, Guo Feng at last returned from the Uyghur court.

sentences.zh: 十一月，庚午，上祀圓丘。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day gengwu, the Emperor sacrificed at the Round Mound.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the day gengwu, the Emperor performed the sacrifice at the Round Mound.

sentences.zh: 上屢詔李納以棣州歸王武俊，納百方遷延，請以海州易之於朝廷。

translations.literal: The Emperor repeatedly ordered Li Na to return Di Prefecture to Wang Wujun; Na put it off by every excuse and asked the court to exchange it for Hai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor repeatedly ordered Li Na to return Di Prefecture to Wang Wujun, but Na evaded the command by every possible excuse and asked the court to swap it for Hai Prefecture instead.

sentences.zh: 上不許。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not permit this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 乃請詔武俊先歸田緒四縣，上從之。

translations.literal: He then asked that Wang Wujun first return four counties to Tian Xu; the Emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: Na then asked that Wang Wujun first return four counties to Tian Xu; the Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 十二月，納始以棣州歸武俊。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Na at last returned Di Prefecture to Wujun.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Na at last surrendered Di Prefecture to Wujun.

sentences.zh: 德宗神武聖文皇帝八貞元七年（

translations.literal: Eighth year of Zhenyuan of Emperor Dezong, the Divine Martial Sagely Cultured Sovereign (
translations.idiomatic: Eighth year of Zhenyuan, reign of Emperor Dezong, the Divine Martial Sagely Cultured Sovereign (

sentences.zh: 辛未，公元七九一年）

translations.literal: xinwei, AD 791)
translations.idiomatic: xinwei, AD 791)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，己巳，襄王黃薨。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring, on the day jisi, the Prince of Xiang, Huang, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, on the day jisi, the Prince of Xiang, Huang, died.

sentences.zh: 二月，癸卯，遣鴻臚少卿庾鋌冊回鶻奉誠可汗。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day guimao, the court dispatched Assistant Director of the Court of Diplomatic Reception Yu Ting to invest the Uyghur Fengcheng Khagan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day guimao, the court sent Assistant Director of the Court of Diplomatic Reception Yu Ting to invest the Uyghur Fengcheng Khagan.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，詔涇原節度使劉昌築平涼故城，以扼彈箏峽口。

translations.literal: On the day wuxu, an edict ordered Jingyuan Military Governor Liu Chang to build up the old city of Pingliang to choke off the mouth of Danzheng Gorge.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuxu, an edict ordered Jingyuan Military Governor Liu Chang to rebuild the old city of Pingliang and seal the mouth of Danzheng Gorge.

sentences.zh: 浹辰而畢，分兵戍之。

translations.literal: In twelve days it was finished; troops were divided to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: The work was finished in twelve days, and garrisons were posted throughout.

sentences.zh: 昌又築朝谷堡。

translations.literal: Chang also built Chaogu Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Chang also built Chaogu Fort.

sentences.zh: 甲子，詔名其堡曰彰信，涇原稍安。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi, an edict named the fort Zhangxin; Jingyuan gradually settled.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiazi, an edict named the fort Zhangxin, and Jingyuan gradually grew secure.

sentences.zh: 初，上還長安，以神策等軍有衛從之勞，皆賜名興元元從奉天定難功臣，以官領之，撫恤優厚。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Emperor returned to Chang'an, because the Shence and other armies had labored in guarding and escorting him, they were all granted the title of Meritorious Ministers Who Accompanied [Him] at Xingyuan and Quelled the Difficulty at Fengtian, led by officials, and treated with generous care and favor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor first returned to Chang'an, he rewarded the Shence and other armies for their service in guarding and escorting him by granting them all the title of Meritorious Ministers Who Accompanied Him at Xingyuan and Quelled the Crisis at Fengtian. Officials were appointed to lead them, and they received lavish care and favor.

sentences.zh: 禁軍恃恩驕橫，侵暴百姓，陵忽府縣，至詬辱官吏，毀裂案牘。

translations.literal: The imperial guard relied on imperial favor and grew arrogant; they brutalized common people, bullied prefectural and county offices, even reviling officials and tearing up documents.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial guard, emboldened by imperial favor, grew arrogant and violent. They preyed on common people, trampled prefectural and county offices, reviled officials, and even tore up official documents.

sentences.zh: 府縣官有不勝忿而刑之者，朝笞一人，夕貶萬里，由是府縣雖有公嚴之官，莫得舉其職。

translations.literal: When a prefectural or county official, unable to restrain his anger, punished one of them, by morning he would be flogged and by evening exiled ten thousand li away; thus though there were upright and stern officials in the prefectures and counties, none could perform their duties.
translations.idiomatic: If a prefectural or county official, unable to contain his rage, punished a guardsman, that official would be flogged by morning and exiled ten thousand li by evening. Though upright and stern men still held office in the prefectures and counties, none could do his job.

sentences.zh: 市井富民，往往行賂寄名軍籍，則府縣不能制。

translations.literal: Wealthy men of the marketplace often bribed their way onto military rolls, and then the prefectures and counties could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy merchants often bribed their way onto military rolls, and once enrolled they were beyond the reach of prefectural and county authority.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，詔：神威、六軍吏士與百姓訟者，委之府縣，小事牒本軍，大事奏聞。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi, an edict declared: disputes between officers and men of the Shenwei and Six Armies and common people shall be entrusted to prefectures and counties; minor matters shall be reported to their own army, major ones reported to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinsi, an edict declared that lawsuits between officers and men of the Shenwei and Six Armies and common people were to be handled by prefectures and counties; minor cases were to be reported to the soldier's own army, major ones to the throne.

sentences.zh: 若軍士陵忽府縣，禁身以聞，委御史臺推覆。

translations.literal: If soldiers bully prefectures and counties, they shall be detained and the matter reported; investigation shall be entrusted to the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: If soldiers bullied prefectural or county offices, they were to be detained pending report, and the Censorate was to investigate.

sentences.zh: 縣吏輒敢笞辱，必從貶謫。

translations.literal: If county clerks dare to flog or humiliate [soldiers], they shall without exception be demoted and exiled.
translations.idiomatic: Any county clerk who dared beat or humiliate a soldier was to be demoted and exiled without exception.

sentences.zh: 癸未，易定節度使張孝忠薨。

translations.literal: On the day guimao, Yiding Military Governor Zhang Xiaozhong died.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guimao, Yiding Military Governor Zhang Xiaozhong died.

sentences.zh: 安南都護高正平重賦斂，夏，四月，群蠻酋長杜英翰等起兵圍都護府，正平以憂死。

translations.literal: Protector-General of Annan Gao Zhengping heavily taxed and levied; in the fourth month of summer, tribal chiefs including Du Yinghan raised troops and besieged the Protector-General's headquarters; Zhengping died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: Protector-General of Annan Gao Zhengping imposed crushing taxes and levies. In the fourth month of summer, tribal chiefs led by Du Yinghan rose in arms and besieged the Protector-General's headquarters. Zhengping died of grief.

sentences.zh: 群蠻聞之皆降。

translations.literal: When the tribes heard of this, they all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the tribes heard of his death, they all submitted.

sentences.zh: 五月，辛巳，置柔遠軍於安南。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day xinsi, the Rouyuan Army was established in Annan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the day xinsi, the Rouyuan Army was established in Annan.

sentences.zh: 端王遇薨。

translations.literal: The Prince of Duan, Yu, died.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Duan, Yu, died.

sentences.zh: 韋皋比年致書招雲南王異牟尋，終未獲報。

translations.literal: Wei Gao for years sent letters to win over the King of Nanzhao, Yimouxun, but never received a reply.
translations.idiomatic: For years Wei Gao had sent letters seeking to win over the King of Nanzhao, Yimouxun, yet never received an answer.

sentences.zh: 然吐蕃每發雲南兵，雲南與之益少。

translations.literal: Yet whenever Tibet mobilized Nanzhao's troops, Nanzhao sent fewer and fewer.
translations.idiomatic: Yet whenever Tibet called on Nanzhao for troops, Nanzhao sent fewer and fewer men.

sentences.zh: 皋知異牟尋心附於唐，討擊副使段忠義，本閣羅鳳使者也。

translations.literal: Gao knew Yimouxun's heart inclined toward Tang; Suppression and Attack Deputy Commissioner Duan Zhongyi had originally been an envoy of Geluofeng.
translations.idiomatic: Gao knew Yimouxun's heart leaned toward Tang. Suppression and Attack Deputy Commissioner Duan Zhongyi had once served as an envoy of Geluofeng.

sentences.zh: 六月，丙申，皋遣忠義還雲南，並致書敦諭之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day bingshen, Gao sent Zhongyi back to Nanzhao and also sent a letter urging and instructing him.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the day bingshen, Gao sent Zhongyi back to Nanzhao with a letter urging and instructing Yimouxun.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，戊寅，以定州刺史張升雲為義武留後。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on the day wuyin, Zhang Shengyun, Prefect of Ding Prefecture, was made acting military governor of Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on the day wuyin, Zhang Shengyun, Prefect of Ding Prefecture, was appointed acting military governor of Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，以虔州刺史趙昌為安南都護，群蠻遂安。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen, Zhao Chang, Prefect of Qian Prefecture, was made Protector-General of Annan, and the tribes settled down.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengchen, Zhao Chang, Prefect of Qian Prefecture, was appointed Protector-General of Annan, and the tribes were pacified.

sentences.zh: 八月，丙午，以翰林學士陸贄為兵部侍郎，餘職皆解。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day bingwu, Hanlin Academician Lu Zhi was appointed Vice Minister of War; all his other posts were removed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the day bingwu, Hanlin Academician Lu Zhi was appointed Vice Minister of War, and all his other offices were stripped away.

sentences.zh: 竇參惡之也。

translations.literal: Dou Can hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Can had engineered this out of hatred for him.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃攻靈州，為回鶻所敗，夜遁。

translations.literal: Tibet attacked Ling Prefecture, was defeated by the Uyghurs, and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet attacked Ling Prefecture, was defeated by the Uyghurs, and fled under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 九月，回鶻遣使來獻俘。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the Uyghurs sent envoys to present captives.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, the Uyghurs sent envoys to present captives to the court.

sentences.zh: 冬，十二月，甲午，又遣使獻所獲吐蕃酋長尚結心。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of winter, on the day jiawu, they again sent envoys to present the captured Tibetan chieftain Shang Jiexin.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of winter, on the day jiawu, they again sent envoys to present the captured Tibetan chieftain Shang Jiexin.

sentences.zh: 福建觀察使吳湊，為治有聲，竇參以私憾毀之，且言其病風。

translations.literal: Fujian Observation Commissioner Wu Cou had a reputation for good governance; Dou Can slandered him out of personal resentment and also claimed he had wind sickness.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian Observation Commissioner Wu Cou was widely praised for his governance, but Dou Can slandered him out of private spite and claimed he suffered from paralysis.

sentences.zh: 上召至京師，使之步以察之，知參之誣，由是始惡參。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned him to the capital and had him walk so as to observe him; knowing Can had lied, the Emperor from this point began to dislike Can.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor summoned Cou to the capital and had him walk so he could see for himself. Realizing Dou Can had lied, the Emperor began to turn against Can.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，以湊為陝虢觀察使以代參黨李翼。

translations.literal: On the day dingyou, Cou was made Shaan-Guo Observation Commissioner, replacing Li Yi, a member of Can's faction.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingyou, Cou was appointed Shaan-Guo Observation Commissioner, replacing Li Yi, a member of Dou Can's faction.

sentences.zh: 睦王述薨。

translations.literal: The Prince of Mu, Shu, died.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Mu, Shu, died.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃知韋皋使者在雲南，遣使讓之。

translations.literal: Learning that Wei Gao's envoy was in Nanzhao, Tibet sent an envoy to rebuke them.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibet learned that Wei Gao's envoy was in Nanzhao, it sent an envoy to rebuke the Nanzhao court.

sentences.zh: 雲南王異牟尋紿之曰：「唐使，本蠻也，皋聽其歸耳，無它謀也。

translations.literal: King Yimouxun of Nanzhao deceived them, saying: 'The Tang envoy is originally one of our own barbarians; Gao merely allowed him to return home—there is no other plot.
translations.idiomatic: King Yimouxun of Nanzhao deceived them, saying, 'The Tang envoy is one of our own people. Gao simply let him come home. There is no other scheme.

sentences.zh: 」因執以送吐蕃。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon he seized him and handed him over to Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Then he seized the envoy and handed him over to Tibet.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃多取其大臣之子為質，雲南愈怨。

translations.literal: Tibet frequently took the sons of Nanzhao ministers as hostages; Nanzhao grew ever more resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet repeatedly took the sons of Nanzhao ministers as hostages, and Nanzhao's resentment deepened.

sentences.zh: 勿鄧酋長苴夢沖，潛通吐蕃，扇誘群蠻，隔絕雲南使者。

translations.literal: Wudeng chieftain Jumengchong secretly communicated with Tibet, incited the tribal peoples, and cut off Nanzhao's envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Wudeng chieftain Jumengchong secretly colluded with Tibet, stirred up the tribal peoples, and blocked Nanzhao's envoys.

sentences.zh: 韋皋遣三部落總管蘇峞將兵至琵琶川。

translations.literal: Wei Gao dispatched the Three-Tribes Commander Su Wei to lead troops to Pipa River.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gao dispatched Three-Tribes Commander Su Wei to lead troops to Pipa River.

translations.idiomatic: CATEGORY: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
